item.title: Dr Zubaida Rahman: No woman should be left behind in fight against cancer
item.description:
Vice-President of the Ziaur Rahman Foundation Dr Zubaida Rahman on Thursday called for ensuring accessible and affordable healthcare services for women to prevent and combat female cancers, stressing that no woman should be left behind in the fight against the disease.
"We aspire to prevent what we can, diagnose early, treat effectively and reduce avoidable suffering. No patient should be left behind," she said.
Zubaida Rahman, wife of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, made the remarks while addressing the inaugural ceremony of the 11th Bangladesh International Cancer Congress (BICC) 2026 at Radisson Blu Water Garden Hotel in the capital as the chief guest.
The two-day congress, being held on November 19-20, has brought together around 1,000 distinguished oncologists, including 40 foreign experts, healthcare professionals, researchers and other stakeholders to discuss the latest developments in cancer prevention, diagnosis, treatment and research.
Highlighting the need to protect women from cancer, Dr Zubaida said women account for 50.8% of the country's population and stressed the importance of taking effective measures to save mothers and sisters from deadly female cancers.
"Millions of women in our cities and villages silently suffer in pain, putting their healthcare at the bottom of their family's priority list," she said, underscoring the need to raise awareness and ensure access to health check-ups and medical facilities.
She said the goal should be to build a healthcare system where everyone receives treatment with dignity and respect and every person's health is given priority in the fight against cancer.
Emphasizing timely healthcare services, she said a woman's right to live must never depend on where she lives.
Zubaida called for ensuring vaccination for girls both inside and outside schools and expanding cancer screening facilities to women in urban and rural communities across the country.
She stressed that every positive screening result must be followed by proper diagnosis and treatment, while affordable healthcare, effective referral systems and trained medical personnel are essential to prevent patients from being lost between clinics and hospitals.
She also called for expanding healthcare services through schools, community clinics and local hospitals rather than confining them to specialized medical centers.
Dr Zubaida said community health workers and primary healthcare teams could play a vital role in raising awareness among women, guiding them through screening programs and connecting them with referral services.
She emphasized stronger cooperation among the government, healthcare professionals, cancer survivors, civil society and development partners to make cancer care accessible to all.
The success of such initiatives, she said, should be measured by the number of girls vaccinated, women screened, cancers detected at an early stage, patients receiving timely treatment and families protected from unbearable healthcare expenses.

item.title: Ex-state minister Shahriar Alam's house set ablaze in Rajshahi
item.description:
A fire broke out at the house of former state minister for foreign affairs Shahriar Alam in Bagha Upazila of Rajshahi on Thursday.
The incident took place at his residence in Chaksinga village under Arani municipality.
Eyewitnesses said a group of five to six people arrived on motorcycles, climbed over the boundary wall and entered the property. They allegedly poured petrol inside the house and set it on fire. The flames quickly spread, prompting local residents to gather and put out the fire with water after the attackers left.
A video circulating on social media appeared to show flames burning on the ground floor of the four-storey house.
However, Bagha Police Station Officer-in-Charge Serajul Haque said some youths had attempted to set fire to the property, but locals prevented them from entering by stopping them at the boundary wall. He said the youths set fire to the house’s gate, which residents quickly extinguished.
The fire service was not called to the scene. The extent of the damage could not immediately be determined.

item.title: Actress Jyotika Jyoti sent to jail in July murder case
item.description:
Actress Jyotika Jyoti has been sent to jail in a case filed over the attempted murder of Enamul Haque in Dhaka’s Bhatara area during the July 2024 uprising.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ashraful Haque passed the order on Thursday following an application by the investigation officer, said SI Kamal Uddin of the prosecution department.
Sub-Inspector Murshidul Alam of the Detective Branch’s Gulshan Zonal Team, the investigation officer, produced Jyoti before the court and sought an order to keep her in custody.
Jyoti was brought to the courtroom during the hearing and was seen in tears. No lawyer appeared on her behalf. Dhaka Metropolitan Public Prosecutor Omar Faruqui represented the state.
Jyoti is listed as accused No 216 in the case.
Earlier, a team of the DB’s Uttara Division arrested her during a raid on a house in Sector 18 of Uttara, under Turag Police Station, around 2:30am on Thursday, acting on a tip-off.
According to the case statement, protesters gathered in front of Bhatara Police Station on July 19, 2024, during the uprising, when police allegedly opened fire. Enamul was shot in the leg and received treatment at a hospital.
He later filed a case with a Dhaka court against 283 named accused, including former prime minister and Awami League president Sheikh Hasina, and 300-400 unidentified people.
Seventeen entertainment personalities, including actors Apu Biswas, Ashna Habib Bhabna, Nusrat Faria, Zayed Khan and Jyoti, were also named as accused. The complaint alleged that they had opposed the anti-discrimination student movement and provided financial support to the Awami League.
Apu Biswas and Nusrat Faria are currently on bail in the case.

item.title: Ex-land minister Javed jailed for 15yrs over Tk25cr loan scam
item.description:
A court in Chittagong on Thursday sentenced former land minister Saifuzzaman Chowdhury Javed to 15 years in prison for embezzling Tk25 crore in loans from United Commercial Bank Limited (UCBL) and laundering the money abroad.
The court also fined him Tk50 crore.
Judge Mizanur Rahman of the Divisional Special Judge’s Court delivered the verdict, sentencing 17 of the 36 accused to different prison terms and acquitting the remaining 19.
Among those convicted was Javed’s wife, Rukmila Zaman, a former UCBL chairperson, along with several former bank directors, officials and executives of the Aramit Group.
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) filed the case, in which 56 witnesses testified during the trial.
According to the charge sheet, the loan was obtained through a shell company, Vision Trading, using Aramit Group protocol officer Mohammad Farman Ullah as a fictitious businessman.
The alleged irregularities took place between October 13, 2019, and February 13, 2020. Vision Trading was registered using false information before opening an account at UCBL’s Port branch in Chittagong. It later sought a 180-day loan, claiming the money would be used to import wheat, turmeric, chickpeas and peas.
The charge sheet said the bank’s board approved the loan despite negative assessments and without proper scrutiny. The funds were disbursed through pay orders to four entities and subsequently withdrawn or transferred to other accounts.
The ACC alleged that Javed used employees to withdraw the money and send it abroad through the informal hundi system to acquire overseas assets. Some of the funds were also deposited into accounts of Aramit Cement and Aramit Thai Aluminium Limited to repay their existing loans.
ACC Deputy Director Md Mashiur Rahman filed the case on July 24, 2025. The commission submitted its charge sheet on January 5 this year, naming 36 accused. The court accepted it two days later and framed charges on March 11.
The trial began on April 5 with the recording of the complainant’s testimony. The charge sheet listed 92 witnesses.

item.title: Purbachal plot scam: Partex founder’s son Rubel sent to jail
item.description:
Ashfaq Aziz Rubel, son of late Partex Group founder chairman MA Hashem, has been sent to jail after a Dhaka court rejected his bail petition in a corruption case over plot allocation in Rajuk’s Purbachal Residential Project.
Rubel, who was sentenced to 14 years in prison in the case, surrendered before Dhaka Special Judge Court-9 on November 17 and sought bail pending an appeal against the verdict.
After a hearing, Judge Md Abdus Salam rejected his bail petition and ordered him to be sent to jail.
Saiful Islam Mithu, bench assistant of the court, confirmed the matter on Thursday.
He said Rubel’s lawyers had sought bail pending an appeal against the verdict and requested first-class prison division for him. The court, however, rejected the bail plea and ordered his imprisonment.
On October 13, the same court sentenced eight people, including Rubel, to 14 years in prison each in the case.
The convicts are former Rajuk chairman Iqbal Uddin Chowdhury; former Rajuk members SD Foyez, AKM Wahedul Islam, SM Zafar Ullah, HM Zahurul Haque and Md Rezaul Karim Tarafdar; and Partex Group founder chairman MA Hashem’s two sons, Shawkat Aziz Russell and Ashfaq Aziz Rubel.
The court also fined each of the convicts Tk20 lakh.
According to the verdict, Rubel and Russell were found guilty under Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, and Section 409 of the Penal Code. They were sentenced to seven years of rigorous imprisonment under each section, totalling 14 years and fined Tk20 lakh each. In default of payment, they will serve an additional year in prison.
The six former Rajuk officials were also sentenced to 14 years of rigorous imprisonment each and fined Tk20 lakh each under the same provisions. They will face an additional year in prison if they fail to pay the fines.
The court ordered that the sentences under the two sections run concurrently and that time already spent in custody be deducted from the total sentences.
The accused were, however, acquitted of charges under Section 420 of the Penal Code due to a lack of evidence.
The court also ordered the cancellation of two plots allotted to Russell and Rubel in Sector 1, Road 405, under plot numbers 011 and 013, and their confiscation in favour of the state.
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) filed the case on February 8, 2017, over allegations that the accused abused their influence to secure two 10-katha plots, totalling 20 kathas, in Purbachal for the two brothers.
The case was filed by then ACC Assistant Deputy Director Sylvia Ferdous. According to the complaint, the accused acted in collusion to allocate the plots to Russell and Rubel, causing losses to the state.
Meanwhile, Russell surrendered before the same court on November 1 and sought bail pending an appeal against the verdict. The court rejected his petition and sent him to jail. He later secured six months’ bail from the High Court on November 10.

item.title: 96 BGB platoons deployed as Dhaka braces for Awami League lockdown
item.description:
Security has been tightened across Dhaka, with law enforcement agencies on high alert as the Awami League, whose activities are banned, observes a dawn-to-dusk “lockdown” programme on Thursday.
Although the pre-announced programme has triggered anxiety among some people, there was no visible impact on public life in the capital. Long-distance buses continued to operate from Gabtoli and Sayedabad, while inter-district services also entered Dhaka as usual.
Police have stepped up intelligence surveillance and security measures over concerns about possible sabotage, attacks on public and private establishments, and attempts to spread panic.
Officials at Police Headquarters said security personnel had been placed on high alert at key points across the country, taking intelligence reports and possible plans for sabotage into account. Police would act firmly against attempts to create panic through vandalism or crude bomb explosions, they said.
The police headquarters said police, the SRB and other law enforcement agencies were maintaining heightened vigilance, while plainclothes intelligence personnel were monitoring different areas and important installations.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police Additional Deputy Commissioner (Media) Niaz Mehedi said police were taking action against those attempting to spread panic through arson and violence.
Wing Commander M Z M Intekhab Chowdhury, director of the SRB’s legal and media wing, said the force was prepared to prevent any attempt at sabotage or violence.
Meanwhile, a total of 96 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed in Dhaka, Chittagong, Narayanganj, Gazipur, Gopalganj, Mymensingh and Faridpur to maintain law and order and ensure public safety.
Deployed on the instructions of the home ministry, BGB personnel are working in coordination with district administrations and other law enforcement agencies. They are maintaining security at key installations and industrial areas and monitoring the situation to prevent disorder and violence.
BGB Headquarters said its monitoring cell was using technology to oversee developments on the ground, with live footage from drones, body-worn cameras and improvised devices being monitored round the clock.

item.title: PM: Bangladesh to launch locally developed satellite within 3 years
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday said Bangladesh aims to launch a locally developed satellite into space within the next three years, with a team of Bangladeshi scientists working on the project.
“Within the next three years, we will send our own satellite into space, InshaAllah. Our own scientists are working on it. Not a single foreigner is involved. They are all Bangladeshi scientists,” he said.
The prime minister made the announcement while inaugurating the National Aero-Genius Competition-2026, organised by Aviation and Aerospace University, Bangladesh, in Lalmonirhat.
Tarique said the government has also set aside Tk500 crore to support young researchers and innovators, adding that more funds would be allocated if necessary to ensure that promising innovations do not fail because of a lack of money.
Addressing the young participants, Tarique said the competition has strengthened his confidence in the country's potential to make progress in aviation, aerospace and other fields of innovation.
He said the country's young generation could bring about breakthroughs in different areas of global innovation if provided with quality education, research opportunities, modern laboratories and incubation facilities.
“Science and technology will shape the world of tomorrow. Falling behind in science and technology means falling behind as individuals and as a country,” Tarique said, urging students to prepare themselves to compete globally.
He said the government has set a target of turning Bangladesh into one of the leading aviation hubs in South and Southeast Asia by 2034.
The prime minister expressed confidence that Aviation and Aerospace University, Bangladesh, the country's only specialised university in the sector, would play a significant role in achieving the target.
He said aviation was no longer merely a means of transport but also a driving force behind international trade, tourism, healthcare, education, diplomacy and economic development.
The prime minister urged students to go beyond being users of technology and become innovators, saying the country's geographical location, growing economy and expanding international trade offered significant opportunities for the aviation and aerospace sectors.
He encouraged young researchers to think beyond traditional approaches, develop new ideas and turn their innovations into practical solutions that could improve communication, support agriculture, help manage disasters and make people's lives safer and more comfortable.
Tarique also stressed the need to maintain continuity in research and innovation initiatives, saying the government would extend support to young scientists and students.
He said the competition should not remain limited to exhibitions and contests but should help bring new inventions into practical use.
The prime minister expressed hope that the initiative would contribute to the development of Bangladesh's own space technology, drone industry and research activities.
He said the country needed to develop technologies of its own rather than remain only a user of innovations made elsewhere.
Tarique urged the students to have confidence in their abilities, saying their talent and creativity could help build a prosperous, self-reliant and technology-driven Bangladesh.
Later, the prime minister visited the university campus.
The prime minister planted a tree on the university campus.
The competition features 74 teams comprising 296 young innovators from across the country, competing in four categories: fixed-wing UAV, rotorcraft, space robotics and soccer bots.
Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon, Disaster Management and Relief Minister and Lalmonirhat-3 MP Asadul Habib Dulu and Aviation and Aerospace University, Bangladesh Vice-Chancellor Air Vice Marshal M Mustafizur Rahman, among others, spoke at the programme.

item.title: Tareen alleges forged documents used in bid to remove her as Ittefaq publisher
item.description:
Tareen Hossain has protested an alleged attempt to remove her as publisher of The Daily Ittefaq through a fake application and forged documents.
In a statement issued on Thursday, Tareen said she had never applied to the Dhaka District Magistrate’s Office to change the newspaper’s publisher, signed any related documents or authorised anyone to initiate such a process.
She described the application allegedly submitted in her name as fabricated and forged, saying any approval granted on its basis would be legally and administratively invalid.
The statement said Ittefaq Group of Publications Limited Chairman Anwar Hossain Manju and the newspaper’s editor, Tasmima Hossain, were also unaware of the alleged process.
It added that the purported forgery had taken place without the knowledge of any member of the company’s board of directors.
Currently abroad, Tareen urged the authorities concerned to immediately verify the authenticity and source of the application submitted in her name.
The statement also disputed reports published by several media outlets on November 18 regarding the proposed change of publisher, accusing them of presenting inaccurate and misleading information about her political affiliation, the newspaper’s financial transactions and its board of directors.
Tareen denied claims that she was a presidium member of the Bangladesh Awami Jubo League, saying she had never held such a position or been a member of the organisation.
She also rejected allegations that a significant portion of the newspaper’s revenue had been deposited into her personal bank account.
According to the statement, revenue from the newspaper’s digital operations was deposited into Ittefaq’s official corporate bank account.
The statement further clarified that her former husband was not a member of The Daily Ittefaq’s board of directors, contrary to claims made in the reports.
The newspaper’s management urged the media outlets concerned to correct the disputed information and refrain from publishing further misleading reports about Tareen and The Daily Ittefaq.
It also criticised the outlets for publishing reports without proper fact-checking or seeking comments from the relevant authorities, saying such practices were contrary to professional journalistic standards.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune, Tareen said the matter was not a dispute between a father and daughter.
“Both my father and I were unaware that this application had been filed,” she said.

item.title: MP’s residence, police station, Grameen Bank branch torched in Gopalganj
item.description:
An angry mob attacked the residence of Selimuzzaman Selim, MP for the Gopalganj-1 constituency, in Kashiani, Gopalganj, hurling crude bombs, vandalising the property and setting it on fire on Thursday morning.
The attackers reportedly used petrol to set the house ablaze at around 10:30am.
Meanwhile, Muksudpur police station and a Grameen Bank branch were also vandalised and set on fire allegedly by Awami League activists and supporters.
Although no fresh incidents of violence had been reported in Gopalganj since Wednesday night, tension remained high across the district. Traffic on town roads was sparse, while shops remained closed.
Since early Thursday morning, protesters have blocked the Gopalganj sections of the Dhaka-Khulna and Dhaka-Barisal highways by felling trees across the roads, halting vehicular movement. Barricades have also been set up on several internal roads across the district.
Traffic has remained suspended across Gopalganj town and its internal road network since morning. Residents have been avoiding going outdoors unless necessary, while businesses remain shut.
The Gopalganj-Pirojpur regional highway has also remained blocked since the night of November 17, with tree trunks placed across the road at several locations in Tungipara.
No security checkpoints were seen at key locations in the town on Wednesday, while members of the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), Armed Police Battalion (APBn) and Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Party (VDP) were seen stationed at the deputy commissioner's office.

item.title: Warming Bay of Bengal threatens fishing livelihoods along Bangladesh coast
item.description:
For thousands of fishing families along Bangladesh’s coast, the Bay of Bengal is more than a source of food. It is their workplace, their primary source of income and the foundation of generations of traditional livelihoods.
But the changing ocean is creating new uncertainties. Rising sea temperatures, shifting marine ecosystems, changing salinity and increasingly unpredictable weather are adding pressure to fishing communities already struggling with limited resources, rising operating costs and declining livelihood security.
The consequences extend beyond fishermen at sea. Women involved in fish processing, drying and trading, boat workers, transporters and coastal markets also depend on the stability of marine fisheries.
As world leaders and negotiators gather at the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, the challenges facing Bangladesh's coastal communities raise an important question: how can climate finance and adaptation policies protect people whose livelihoods depend directly on a changing ocean?
The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) says the ocean has absorbed more than 90% of the excess heat accumulated in the climate system. This warming affects marine ecosystems, including the distribution, reproduction and survival of fish species.
Warmer water can alter fish migration patterns and breeding conditions. It can also reduce dissolved oxygen, while increasing carbon dioxide absorption contributes to ocean acidification, affecting organisms that form shells and other parts of the marine food chain.
For Bangladesh, these changes matter because the country's coastal economy and food security are closely connected to the Bay of Bengal and its estuarine systems.
According to the Department of Fisheries' Yearbook of Fisheries Statistics 2023–24, Bangladesh produced approximately 5.02 million tonnes of fish. Marine fisheries contributed around 640,000 tonnes, while inland fisheries and aquaculture accounted for most of the remaining production.
Although marine fisheries represent a smaller share of national production, they support coastal employment, local economies and the country's supply of important fish species.
However, climate change is not the only pressure. Overfishing, illegal fishing, pollution, habitat degradation and inadequate fisheries management also affect marine resources. Distinguishing the contribution of each factor requires long-term scientific monitoring.
Water resources and environmental expert Dr Ainun Nishat emphasises the importance of understanding the connection between rivers, estuaries and the sea.
The northern Bay of Bengal receives freshwater and sediment from Bangladesh's extensive river network. Changes in river flows, sediment movement and salinity can influence coastal habitats and the ecological conditions that support fisheries.
The challenge, therefore, cannot be addressed through marine fisheries management alone. River management, coastal protection, freshwater availability and ecosystem conservation must be considered together.
Long-term research is needed to establish how these interacting environmental changes are affecting fish habitats and coastal livelihoods.
For small-scale fishermen, environmental changes can translate directly into financial insecurity.
Unpredictable fishing conditions may force them to travel farther, spend more on fuel and ice, and remain at sea longer without certainty about their catch. When fishing trips fail, families can become more dependent on loans and informal credit.
Women working in fish processing, drying and marketing also face economic consequences when catches become irregular.
Climate and development policy specialist Md Shamsuddoha of the Centre for Participatory Research and Development (CPRD) has highlighted the importance of recognising climate vulnerability as an issue of justice, finance and livelihoods.
The central policy concern is that communities with limited responsibility for global emissions are increasingly exposed to climate-related risks but have fewer resources to respond.
Adaptation finance, he argues in the context of this policy debate, needs to reach the people most affected. Support for resilient fishing infrastructure, marine research, early-warning systems and alternative livelihoods should be part of that response.
Climate-related losses also need attention. When environmental changes gradually undermine traditional livelihoods, the economic consequences may extend beyond immediate disaster damage.
The Bangladesh Oceanographic Research Institute (BORI) has an important role in strengthening the scientific understanding of the Bay of Bengal.
Regular observations of sea temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, ocean currents and marine biodiversity are essential to identify changes in the marine environment.
The Department of Fisheries also needs reliable information on fish stocks, migration patterns and seasonal catches to develop evidence-based management policies.
Government agencies must strengthen coordination among fisheries authorities, oceanographic researchers, meteorological services and coastal disaster management institutions.
For fishing communities, timely marine weather forecasts and accessible early-warning systems can reduce risks to lives and livelihoods.
Dr Nandan Mukherjee, senior lecturer and director of the Binks Institute for Sustainability at the University of Dundee, perspective on climate vulnerability also points to the need for community-centred adaptation. Small-scale fishermen should have a meaningful role in decisions affecting fishing regulations, financial assistance and livelihood support.
The challenges facing Bangladesh's fishing communities are relevant to wider climate negotiations.
At COP31, adaptation finance, climate-related loss and damage, and support for vulnerable developing countries remain important issues. Bangladesh has an opportunity to highlight the economic consequences of ocean warming and the need to include marine livelihoods in national and international climate strategies.
A stronger response would require investment in marine scientific research, sustainable fisheries management, coastal ecosystem restoration, climate-resilient infrastructure and social protection for fishing households.
Regional cooperation among Bay of Bengal countries is also important because fish populations, ocean currents and marine environmental pressures do not follow national borders.
Ultimately, protecting the Bay of Bengal is not only about conserving marine biodiversity. It is also about safeguarding food security, employment and the dignity of coastal communities.
For Bangladesh's fishing families, the future of the ocean and the future of their livelihoods are inseparable.
This story was produced as part of the COP31 Climate Change Media Partnership, a journalism fellowship organised by Internews' Earth Journalism Network, Informed Earth and the Stanley Center for Peace and Security.

item.title: Two brothers among three killed in Chittagong motorcycle crash
item.description:
Three people, including two brothers, were killed and two others injured in a collision between two motorcycles in Hathazari upazila of Chittagong on Thursday afternoon.
The deceased were identified as Iftekhar Mahmud Tushar, 32, and his younger brother Imtiaz Mahmud Irat, 28, sons of Md Harun of Haider Ali Sepahi Bari in Ward 9 of Farhadabad Union, and Fahim, 19, a resident of Hathazari.
The two brothers had returned home from abroad a few days ago.
The accident occurred around 3pm in the Charia Musa's Dokan area of Mirzapur Union on the Hathazari-Nazirhat regional highway. All five people riding the two motorcycles were injured in the collision.
According to police and local sources, Tushar and Irat were travelling from their home in Farhadabad towards Hathazari when their motorcycle collided with another motorcycle heading towards Nazirhat.
The impact threw all five riders onto the road, leaving them seriously injured.
Locals rescued the injured and took them to Hathazari Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared Tushar dead.
As Irat and Fahim's conditions deteriorated, they were referred to Chittagong Medical College Hospital (CMCH) for advanced treatment. However, Irat died on the way, while Fahim succumbed to his injuries shortly after arriving at the hospital.
Dr Sanjida Tabassum, an emergency department physician at Hathazari Upazila Health Complex, told Dhaka Tribune that several people injured in the accident were brought to the hospital.
"One of them was declared dead, while two critically injured patients were referred to CMCH," she said.
Sub-Inspector Mustafizur Rahman of Nazirhat Highway Police told Dhaka Tribune that three people were killed and two others injured in the accident.

item.title: July Movement coordinator Rafi's village home set on fire
item.description:
Khan Talat Mahmud Rafi, a coordinator of the July Movement and senior joint general secretary of the central committee of Jatiya Chhatra Shakti, alleged that his family home was set on fire in Joypur village of Mohanganj upazila, Netrokona, around 3am on Thursday.
At the time, Rafi's parents were sleeping inside the house. However, a neighbour noticed the fire and raised the alarm, allowing family members to extinguish it before it spread. No major damage was reported.
Speaking about the incident, Rafi said: “Awami League terrorists set this fire at my village home. They poured petrol and set fire to the area directly below the house's electricity meter. Through this, they tried to spread the fire throughout the entire house. At the time of the incident, my parents were sleeping inside the house. When a woman from the neighbouring house noticed the matter and shouted, family members woke up. Later, it was possible to bring the fire under control before it spread. My sleeping parents narrowly escaped with their lives.”
In a Facebook post on Thursday morning, Rafi also alleged that Awami League activists had set fire to his village home around 3am on Wednesday night by pouring petrol below the electricity meter.
He wrote: “Fortunately, as the people in the house woke up, Allah saved my father and mother.”
He further wrote: “My mother called me and said, ‘Do not be afraid, son. We have never harmed anyone. Allah will save us.’ May Allah protect my father and mother.”
Rafi also shared several pictures of the incident in the post.
Mohanganj police station Officer-in-Charge Hafizul Islam Harun told Dhaka Tribune: “We learned that someone attempted to set fire to coordinator Rafi's house at around 3am last night. As family members woke up at the time, they could not set the house on fire further. Hearing the shouting, people from nearby also came forward. There was no significant damage. Evidence has been recovered from the scene. The matter is being investigated. Efforts are underway to identify those involved in the incident.”

Turning down the noise
Law enforcement requires genuine reform
Law minister: Govt has information on network behind crude bomb, arson attacks
Ex-MP Haji Rahim Ullah's ancestral home looted, set fire in Feni
item.description:
Unidentified miscreants looted and set fire to the ancestral residence of former Feni-3 member of parliament Haji Rahim Ullah at Sonapur village in Sonagazi upazila of Feni early Thursday.
Rahim Ullah’s brother-in-law Rafiqul Islam, who was alone in the house, said 15 to 20 armed miscreants scaled the wall, looted valuable belongings, and poured petrol to set fire to three rooms of the multi-story house and three trucks parked outside.
Local residents rushed to the spot and managed to bring the flames under control, said Sonagazi Fire Service Acting Station Officer Md. Nurul Alam.
Sonagazi Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Abul Hashim said police visited the scene.
Haji Rahim Ullah is a former president of the Jeddah chapter of the Awami League. He was elected MP from Feni-3 constituency as an independent candidate in the 10th parliamentary election in 2014.
He has been in jail since his arrest in Dhaka’s Dhanmondi area in October 2024.

item.title: AB Party chairman’s car set ablaze in Bijoynagar
item.description:
Miscreants set fire to the parked car of Amar Bangladesh (AB) Party Chairman Mujibur Rahman Manju in the capital’s Bijoynagar early Thursday.
The incident took place at around 3am beneath the party’s central office, said Azadul Islam Azad, the party’s assistant publicity secretary, in a statement.
According to the party, several masked men arrived in an autorickshaw, poured an inflammable substance from a bottle over Manju’s parked car and set it on fire before fleeing the scene.
The party’s night guards spotted the incident on CCTV cameras and rushed to extinguish the flames. However, part of the vehicle had already been damaged.
In a joint statement issued on Thursday, AB Party Senior Vice-Chairman Professor Dr Major (retd) Abdul Wahab Minar and General Secretary Barrister Asaduzzaman Fuad condemned the attack.
They said setting fire to a political party chairman’s car in the middle of the night was not an isolated incident but a direct assault on political tolerance, democratic values and the country’s political environment.
The leaders said such cowardly attacks and acts of terrorism would not intimidate or silence the AB Party. They added that resorting to arson would only further alienate fascist forces from the people.
They also alleged that the ousted fascist forces had carried out the attack as part of an attempt to destabilise the country.
Describing arson, attacks and intimidation as unacceptable means of suppressing political opponents, they urged the government to take a firm stance against such crimes to protect the country’s democratic environment and political stability.
The two leaders called on law enforcement agencies to conduct a thorough investigation, analyse CCTV footage, identify and arrest those responsible, and ensure exemplary punishment.

item.title: ILO urges dialogue to end RMG wage unrest
item.description:
The International Labour Organization (ILO) has urged the government, garment manufacturers and workers’ representatives to resolve the ongoing minimum wage dispute in Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) sector through evidence-based negotiations and sustained dialogue.
In a statement issued on Thursday, the ILO said it was closely monitoring the wage review and related unrest, expressing concern over reports of violence, vandalism and disruptions affecting workers, businesses and industrial relations.
The organisation welcomed the government’s formation of the Minimum Wage Board, describing consultation among employers and workers as essential to a credible wage-setting process.
Citing the ILO Minimum Wage Fixing Convention, 1970 (No 131), it said wage adjustments should be transparent and based on reliable data, taking into account workers’ living costs, inflation, productivity, employment and the sustainability of businesses.
The ILO also stressed the importance of respecting freedom of association, workers’ right to organise and collective bargaining. It urged all parties to pursue peaceful means to ease tensions and allow the Minimum Wage Board to complete its work.
The organisation reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Bangladesh through technical assistance, research and social dialogue, including efforts to develop an evidence-based, gender-responsive National Wage Policy.

item.title: President: Bangladesh achieves remarkable success in agriculture
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Thursday said Bangladesh has achieved remarkable success in agriculture.
"Although the country faced a huge deficit in food grains immediately after independence, Bangladesh has now been able to increase agricultural production manifold. There is no overall food grain deficit in the country, thanks to the farmers, agricultural scientists and researchers," he said.
The president said this when a delegation from Khulna Agricultural University, led by its Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Md Asaduzzaman Sarker, paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban, said a press release issued by the President's Press Wing.
The president said just after independence, Bangladesh had a population of around 7.5 crore and faced a huge deficit in food grains. "Bangladesh, once known as a food-deficit country, has now been able to increase agricultural production manifold," he said.
The delegation informed the president that Khulna Agricultural University had been able to produce various climate-resilient food crops in the southern region despite several adverse conditions, including climate change and salinity.
During the meeting, the president stressed the effective field-level application of research-based technologies, safe food production and environment-friendly agricultural practices to build a sustainable agricultural system.
He also called for closer coordination among agricultural education, research and extension activities.
At the meeting, the vice-chancellor briefed the president on the university's academic and research activities and its overall progress and invited the president to attend the university's upcoming convocation ceremony. The president accepted the invitation and assured the delegation of his presence at the event.
The President's Military Secretary, Secretary and Press Secretary, along with Treasurer and Registrar of Khulna Agricultural University, were also present.

item.title: Bus, goods-laden truck set on fire in Narayanganj
item.description:
Miscreants set fire to a passenger bus and a straw-laden truck at two separate locations in Narayanganj on Thursday morning.
No casualties were reported.
The incidents took place near Kanchpur Bridge on the Dhaka-Chittagong Highway and at Mirertek Bazar on the Asian Highway.
According to police and local sources, a Tisha Paribahan passenger bus was set on fire on the Dhaka-bound lane near Kanchpur Bridge at around 9:30am. All passengers managed to get off the bus immediately after the fire broke out. However, the bus was extensively damaged.
Kanchpur Highway Police Station Officer-in-Charge Jewel Mia said the damaged bus was removed from the scene using a recovery vehicle. No one was injured in the incident, he added.
Photo: Dhaka Tribune
In a separate incident, a straw-laden truck parked near Mirertek Bazar was set on fire early Thursday.
The truck, carrying straw from Dinajpur, stopped in front of Mirertek Bazar Jame Mosque at around 3:30am. The driver and helper parked beside the road while waiting to unload the cargo and fell asleep inside.
At around 5:30am, a woman passing by noticed the fire and alerted the driver. He tried to extinguish the flames by throwing the burning straw into water beside the road.
Police reached the scene after receiving the information and alerted the Fire Service. A Fire Service team brought the blaze under control at around 7:30am. By then, all the straw on the truck had been destroyed.
Jasim Uddin, in-charge of the Taltala police outpost, said the truck's cargo was destroyed in the fire, but the driver and helper were unharmed.
Those involved would be identified and brought to justice, he added.

item.title: Around 20 factories in Gazipur declare holiday amid workers' unrest
item.description:
Around 20 factories in Gazipur have declared a holiday for Thursday amid ongoing workers' unrest, although the Industrial Police reported closures at five garment factories in Sreepur and the Bhogra Bypass area.
The closures were announced in phases from 8:15am, according to police.
Meanwhile, in the Ansar Road area of Sreepur, leaders and activists of different units of the BNP’s municipal branch, led by its Member Secretary Billal Hossain Bepari, were seen taking positions along the highway and in nearby areas to prevent possible sabotage or unrest.
Police and local residents said workers at Mondol Intimates in the Bagher Bazar area arrived at the factory in the morning and registered their attendance but did not start work. Shortly after 8:15am, they left the premises without management’s permission.
After leaving the factory, the workers gathered at the gate of Golden Refit Garments on the western side of the highway, prompting workers at that factory to come out as well.
The workers then gathered on the highway and demanded the closure of other factories, prompting several establishments in the area to declare a holiday.
Among them were Silken Sewing, Esrotex Garments Ltd in the Notun Bazar area, SM Knit Wear Ltd, Subline Green Tex of Meghna Group in the Sreepur Municipality-Aspada area, Chittagong Denim Ltd in the Gargaria Masterbari area and Meghna Garments.
The workers later moved in groups from Gargaria Masterbari towards Sreepur.
Authorities also declared holidays at around 20 factories along the same road and in nearby areas. These included Crystal Garments, Demimec Garments, Divine Garments, Dhaka Fashion Ltd of Hams Group, Victoria Intimates, Takwa Fashion and Takwa Poshak Kalakan of Palmal Group, the Sustainable Wet Processing Plant, and Meghna Denim and Uniglory Washing Ltd.
Asked about road blockades, Sreepur Upazila Assistant Commissioner (Land) Nahid Niyaz Shishir said the situation had persisted for the past three weeks, with sporadic blockades reported at different locations, including Bangla Bazar in Rajendrapur, Hotapara and Gargaria Masterbari.
Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Amjad Hossain said workers arrived at factories in the morning, registered their attendance and then left without starting work.
He said police intervened when workers later attempted to block the highway towards Sreepur and cleared the road. The situation had since returned to normal.
However, he said authorities had declared holidays at five factories in the Sreepur and Gazipur areas.
A deputy general manager of a garment factory in Bagher Bazar, requesting anonymity, said workers from a neighbouring factory gathered at his factory's gate. As they began pushing against the gate, the management decided to send its own workers home.

item.title: 96 BGB platoons deployed in 7 districts
item.description:
A total of 96 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel have been deployed in seven districts to maintain law and order, ensure public safety and respond to any untoward incidents.
The deployment covers Dhaka, Chittagong, Narayanganj, Gazipur, Gopalganj, Mymensingh and Faridpur.
Of the total, 23 platoons have been deployed in Dhaka, 15 in Chittagong, six in Narayanganj, 15 in Gazipur, 27 in Gopalganj, two in Mymensingh and three in Faridpur. Another five platoons are on standby for deployment.
In a statement on Thursday, BGB said its personnel were operating in coordination with the respective district administrations and other law enforcement agencies, following instructions from the Ministry of Home Affairs.
BGB personnel are strengthening security and surveillance at key installations, industrial zones and other important locations to prevent disorder, violence and activities that could threaten public safety, the statement said.
The BGB headquarters' monitoring cell is also maintaining technology-based surveillance to closely monitor and coordinate the situation on the ground.
Live footage from drones, body-worn cameras and improvised devices is being monitored round the clock, the statement added.

item.title: Tarique reaches Lalmonirhat on daylong visit
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman reached Lalmonirhat by helicopter on Thursday morning on a daylong visit to attend several programmes in the northern district.
He landed at Lalmonirhat Airfield around 10:30am, said his Deputy Press Secretary, Jahidul Islam Rony.
Disaster Management and Relief Minister and Lalmonirhat-3 MP Asadul Habib Dulu, Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Hasan Mahmood Khan, and senior officials of Rangpur Division and Lalmonirhat district welcomed him.
During the visit, Tarique is scheduled to attend the first National Aero-Genius Competition organised by Aviation and Aerospace University, Bangladesh, as the chief guest and visit the university campus.
He will then inaugurate the re-excavation of a drainage canal at Mahendranagar in Lalmonirhat Sadar upazila and exchange views with local beneficiaries.
After a brief stop at Lalmonirhat Circuit House, the prime minister will attend a program titled "Alokito Lalmonirhat" at the district Collectorate Ground.
He is scheduled to return to Dhaka by helicopter on Thursday evening.

item.title: Five burned in gas leak fire at Kathalbagan
item.description:
Five people were burned in a fire caused by a suspected gas leak at a residential building in Kathalbagan, Dhaka, on Thursday morning.
The injured were admitted to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, where three of them are in critical condition.
The fire broke out on the fourth floor of the 10-storey Kanchan Tower in Kathalbagan at around 8:20am on Thursday.
According to the Fire Service media department, two units from the Mohammadpur Fire Station rushed to the scene after receiving the report and began efforts to control the fire.
The blaze was brought under control at 8:45am.
Dr Sultan Mahmud Sikdar, resident surgeon (emergency) at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, said five burn victims were brought to the institute for treatment, three of whom were in critical condition.

item.title: Fire breaks out at Rayerbazar kitchen market
item.description:
A fire broke out at the Rayerbazar kitchen market and several tin-roofed houses beside it in Dhaka on Thursday morning.
The fire started at around 10:20am on Thursday and was brought under control at 10:55am with the efforts of four Fire Service and Civil Defence units.
According to the Fire Service and Civil Defence Media Cell, two units each from the Hazaribagh and Mohammadpur fire stations were dispatched to the scene after receiving reports of the fire. The units arrived at around 10:35am and began working to bring the blaze under control.
The cause of the fire and the extent of the damage could not be immediately determined.
No casualties were reported, the Fire Service said.

item.title: Bangladesh’s coastal communities face funding barriers in climate adaptation
Miscreants set fire to Gazipur Palli Bidyut complaint centre
item.description:
Miscreants set fire to a pile of old wooden materials inside a complaint centre at the Gazipur Palli Bidyut Samity office early Thursday.
The fire broke out at around 3:30am on Thursday at the complaint centre in the Bhurulia area of Gazipur city after two containers of petrol were thrown inside.
Ziaul Haque, deputy general manager of Gazipur Palli Bidyut Samity, said fire service personnel rushed to the scene after receiving the information and brought the fire under control.
Two containers were recovered from the scene. However, it is too early to determine whether they contained petrol or were used in a sabotage attempt without further investigation, he said.
Mohammad Raja Mia, an inspector at Gazipur Fire Service, said three units of the Joydebpur Fire Service brought the fire under control after an hour of efforts.
Old electricity poles and wooden transformer boxes were damaged in the fire.
Aminul Islam, officer-in-charge of Gazipur Metropolitan Police's Sadar police station, said police visited the scene after receiving reports of the incident.

item.title: Panchagarh records season's lowest temperature at 12.5°C
item.description:
Winter is beginning to set in across Panchagarh, with the minimum temperature dropping to 12.5°C on Thursday, the lowest recorded in the district this season.
The Tetulia Weather Observation Centre recorded the temperature at 6am, with relative humidity at 98%.
The minimum temperature fell by 3.2°C in a day, from 15.7°C recorded at 9am on Wednesday.
According to the weather observation centre, the minimum temperature was 17.4°C on Tuesday, 18.5°C on Monday, 16.4°C on Sunday, 15.8°C on Saturday and 15.7°C on Friday. The maximum temperature on Wednesday was 27.6°C.
Local residents said the weather remains warm during the day due to sunshine, but temperatures drop after sunset.
Jitendranath Roy, acting officer-in-charge of the Tetulia Weather Observation Centre, said temperatures may gradually fall further in the coming days.
A mild cold wave may sweep through Panchagarh in December, he added.

item.title: Khulna BNP leaders detain, hand over two youths to police after arson incident
item.description:
Two youths were detained by Khulna district BNP leaders and handed over to police after allegedly setting fire to an area in Gallamari under Labanchara police station in Khulna on Thursday morning.
The detainees were identified as Koushik, 21, and Yasin, 22.
BNP leaders and activists caught the two youths near Labanchara police station while they were fleeing the scene after setting fire. They were later handed over to Labanchara police station.
Khulna district BNP Convener Moniruzzaman Montu, Member Secretary SM Monirul Hasan Bappy and other party leaders and activists were present during the handover.
Labanchara police station Officer-in-Charge Syed Mosharraf Hossain said the two youths were kept in police custody after receiving preliminary medical treatment.
They are being questioned over the incident, while police are investigating whether others were involved, he said.
Further legal action in the case is underway, the OC added.

item.title: Satkhira-Dhaka bus services suspended over security concerns
item.description:
Long-distance bus services on the Satkhira-Dhaka route via the Padma Bridge have been suspended amid fears of road blockades and violence in Gopalganj.
The suspension took effect on Wednesday afternoon, with transport operators confirming that no buses would leave Satkhira for Dhaka on Thursday.
According to transport counter officials, several buses left for Dhaka via the Padma Bridge on Wednesday morning. However, services were suspended from the afternoon following reports of road blockades and unrest at various locations in Gopalganj.
A limited number of buses are operating via an alternative route through Jessore and the Paturia-Daulatdia ferry terminals.
Swadhin, manager of Imad Paribahan's Patkelghata counter, said no buses would operate on the route on Thursday due to security concerns.
Zahir Raihan, manager of SK Paribahan's Satkhira counter, confirmed the suspension, saying drivers, workers and transport owners were concerned following incidents of vehicle arson in different parts of the country.
The sudden suspension has left passengers travelling to Dhaka for urgent work in difficulty. Passengers said alternative routes were increasing both travel time and inconvenience.
Transport operators said services via the Padma Bridge would remain suspended until the situation returned to normal and the administration ensured adequate security.
Bus services from Khulna to Dhaka have also been suspended over the same incident.

item.title: July uprising memorial torched, crude bombs exploded in Tangail
item.description:
Vandals set fire to a memorial dedicated to those killed during the July uprising in Mirzapur upazila of Tangail on Wednesday night.
The incident took place beside the Gorai Highway Police Station, near the Dhaka-Tangail-Jamuna Bridge Highway.
Several crude bombs also exploded near the Gorai flyover and surrounding areas around the same time, triggering panic among locals.
No casualties were reported.
Locals said the vandals set fire to the July uprising martyrs' memorial beside the Gorai Highway Police Station at around 11:30pm. A few minutes later, several crude bombs exploded in succession beneath the Hatur Bhanga flyover in Gorai before the perpetrators fled.
The memorial was completely gutted before police and fire service personnel could reach the scene.
The incident has heightened tensions in the Gorai area.
It is suspected that activists of the Awami League may have carried out the attack ahead of the party's announced lockdown program for Thursday, despite the party's activities being banned.
Mirzapur police station Officer-in-Charge Abdullah Al Mamun said police from Mirzapur and Gorai Highway Police stations rushed to the scene after receiving the information and brought the fire under control.
He added that law enforcement agencies have been conducting regular patrols over the past few days along the Dhaka-Tangail-Jamuna Bridge Highway, the Gorai industrial area, Mirzapur upazila headquarters and other key locations to prevent sabotage.
Police are working to arrest those involved, he said.

item.title: Two BRTC buses torched, railway track set on fire in Rajshahi
item.description:
Vandals set fire to two parked buses at the Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) bus terminal in Rajshahi city and torched a section of railway tracks in Charghat upazila.
Both buses were gutted in the fire at the BRTC terminal in the Am Chattar area under Shah Makhdum police station.
Shah Makhdum police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Akbar Ali confirmed the incident, saying the fire broke out at around 2:25am on Thursday.
According to police, miscreants set fire to the two buses parked at the terminal. Fire service personnel rushed to the scene and brought the blaze under control.
Akbar Ali said police were deployed at the scene immediately after the incident. No one has been arrested in connection with the incident so far.
Meanwhile, a section of railway track was set on fire in Bagmari village under Nimpura Union of Charghat upazila in Rajshahi at around 11:15pm on Wednesday.
Train services on the route remained suspended for an hour before resuming. Locals jointly brought the fire under control after the perpetrators fled.
The Dhaka Commuter train, travelling from Dhaka to Chapainawabganj, was stranded at the affected section.
A team from Charghat Model Police Station headed to the scene after receiving the report. Railway authorities at the local station were also informed to check for any damage to the tracks or technical faults.
Ahmed Hossain Masum, general manager of Bangladesh Railway's Western Zone, said the fire was set in the Bagmari area, east of Nandangachhi Railway Station in Charghat, at around 11:15pm. Train services resumed at 12:05am on Thursday.

29 candidates submit nomination papers for Red Crescent Managing Board election

Tigresses exit Emerging Nations Trophy despite win over Thailand
item.description:
Bangladesh Women's cricket team have been eliminated from the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy despite securing a narrow three-run victory over Thailand in their final group-stage match at Ajman today.
Bangladesh finished level on four points with Zimbabwe in the group but missed out on a place in the Super Six due to an inferior net run rate.
Zimbabwe secured qualification after defeating the Netherlands by 33 runs.
Batting first after losing the toss, Bangladesh struggled early and lost both openers cheaply. Nigar Sultana Joty and Sharmin Akhter attempted to rebuild the innings, with Nigar scoring team-best 45 off 36 balls and Sharmin contributing 16.
Stand-in captain Sobhana Mostary added a valuable 28 off 26 deliveries as Bangladesh posted 132-6 in the stipulated 20 overs.
In pursuit of the 130-run target, Thailand faced early pressure as Bangladesh's Sanjida Akhter Meghla claimed two wickets. However, Nannapat Koncharoenkai and captain Naruemol Chaiwai revived the chase with a 52-run partnership for the third wicket.
Nannapat top-scored with 57, while Naruemol contributed 33 as Thailand remained in contention until the closing stages.
Thailand needed 21 runs from the final two overs but ultimately managed to put up 129-5, falling three runs short of Bangladesh's target.
Despite the victory, Bangladesh's narrow winning margin proved insufficient to improve their net run rate enough to overtake Zimbabwe, bringing their campaign to an end at the group stage.

item.title: Four killed as violence, arson spread ahead of Awami League lockdown
item.description:
At least four people have been killed in separate incidents of political violence and arson in Bangladesh over two days as clashes, crude bomb attacks and widespread destruction intensified ahead of the activities-banned Awami League’s nationwide lockdown on Thursday.
Two BNP-affiliated leaders were killed in Narail on Wednesday evening in an attack allegedly carried out by Awami League activists, while a Krishak Dal leader died in Faridpur on Tuesday night.
A bus helper was also burnt alive in Pirojpur early Wednesday when unidentified assailants torched two parked buses.
The violence extended from Gopalganj, where a police station, security vehicles and BNP lawmakers’ residences were attacked, to several other districts, prompting the deployment of hundreds of additional security personnel.
In Narail’s Kalia upazila, Krishak Dal leader Shahinur Sheikh, 45, and Jatiyatabadi Samajik Sangskritik Sangstha (Jasas) leader Sohel Molla, 35, were killed when attackers assaulted a motorcycle procession organised by BNP-affiliated groups to protest Awami League-linked violence.
The attack occurred at Bottola intersection in Bendar Char on Wednesday evening. Narail Superintendent of Police Mohammad Al Mamun Shikder confirmed the two deaths around 10pm. Several others were injured.
In Faridpur’s Bhanga, Krishak Dal leader Raju Molla died after suffering severe burns during a blockade on the Dhaka-Barishal highway on Tuesday night.
BNP leaders accused Awami League and Chhatra League activists of attacking him and torching motorcycles. Police said efforts were underway to identify those responsible.
In Pirojpur’s Bhandaria, bus helper Mohammad Siam was burnt to death while sleeping inside a parked bus after unidentified attackers set fire to two vehicles around 3:45am Wednesday. Police said the perpetrators had not been identified.
Several shops were also torched in Nazirpur, where attackers targeted a union parishad warehouse containing government-subsidised food supplies.
Gopalganj remained a major flashpoint following Tuesday night’s attacks on Tungipara Police Station, police and Border Guard Bangladesh vehicles, and at least 20 houses, including the residence of BNP lawmaker SM Jilani.
Vehicles are set on fire and barricades are created at several locations along the Dhaka-Khulna highway in Kashiani upazila, including Tarail, Gopalpur, Fokra, Tilchhara and Ghonapara, on Wednesday evening ahead of the November 19 lockdown. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
The violence erupted after police arrested several suspected Awami League and Chhatra League activists. Protesters subsequently stormed the station, vandalised the premises and set vehicles ablaze.
By Wednesday evening, most personnel had reportedly moved from Tungipara Police Station to the district police lines amid fears of renewed attacks. Authorities deployed 21 BGB platoons across Gopalganj to restore security.
In another attack around 8pm Wednesday, unidentified assailants set fire to the front gate of Gopalganj-2 MP Dr KM Babar’s residence and vandalised his personal office.
Patients, including newborns and women recovering from Caesarean sections, fled a clinic housed in the same building. No casualties were reported.
The escalating unrest also disrupted education in Gopalganj, where the local science and technology university announced a two-day closure and postponed examinations. Security was reinforced around the district jail.
Elsewhere, two police officers were injured in Cox’s Bazar’s Ramu when relatives of a Swechchhasebak League leader allegedly attacked police and freed him from custody.
In Khulna, unidentified attackers hurled a crude bomb into the district judge’s court building on Wednesday night, although it failed to explode.
In Rangpur, two buses were set ablaze within 10 hours, with detectives suspecting Chhatra League involvement. The attacks disrupted transport services and spread panic among residents.
Retaliatory violence was also reported against Awami League properties.
In Sirajganj, attackers set fire to the party’s district office and the residence of former lawmaker Habibe Millat Munna.
In Cumilla, the Awami League office and former MP AKM Bahauddin Bahar’s residence were attacked and set ablaze.
Meanwhile, crude bomb explosions and vehicle arson have been reported across at least 28 districts over the past 10 days, according to police figures cited by Reuters. At least 37 Grameen Bank offices have also been targeted since November 10.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed accused Awami League leaders abroad of encouraging violence and warned that those responsible for attacks and sabotage would face prosecution.
The violence has heightened fears of further confrontation as the Awami League prepares to enforce its today’s lockdown, while Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal has announced a procession in Dhaka on Thursday.

item.title: Two BNP leaders killed in attack on rally in Narail
item.description:
Two BNP leaders were killed after activists of the activities-banned Awami League allegedly attacked a BNP procession in Kalia Upazila of Narail on Wednesday evening.
The attack took place around 7pm during a procession organised to protest terrorism and lawlessness.
The deceased were Shahin, general secretary of Kalia Upazila Krishak Dal, and Sohel Molla, general secretary of the upazila unit of Jatiyatabadi Samajik Sangskritik Sangstha (JASAS).
Police and local sources said BNP and its affiliated organisations brought out the procession in Kalia town. Awami League activists allegedly attacked the march, leaving Shahin and Sohel Molla critically injured.
They were taken to hospital, where doctors declared them dead.
Narail Superintendent of Police Mohammad Al Mamun Sikder confirmed the deaths to Bangla Tribune around 10pm.

item.title: Dipu Moni, Sujit Roy Nandi’s homes torched
item.description:
Unidentified attackers set fire to the residences of former education minister Dr Dipu Moni and Awami League organising secretary Sujit Roy Nandi in separate incidents in Chandpur on Wednesday night.
The attacks, reported within half an hour of each other, targeted properties belonging to two senior figures of the activities-banned Awami League.
Around 9pm, attackers allegedly broke into Dipu Moni’s abandoned third-floor residence at Kadamtala Market in the town’s Notun Bazar area and set fire to the premises.
Residents of the building and neighbours extinguished the flames using water.
Advocate Gazi Dulal, who lives on the fifth floor, said the fire caused panic among residents.
He added that the apartment had already been extensively damaged in an arson attack on August 5, 2024, and that Wednesday’s fire mainly affected the remaining debris.
Chandpur Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Fayez Ahmed said he had not received information about the incident but would look into it.
Around 9:30pm, another group of attackers set fire to Sujit Roy Nandi’s two-storey house in Farakkabad village of Chandpur Sadar upazila.
Dipu, a member of Ward 7 of Balia Union Parishad, said the attackers arrived on 40–50 motorcycles before setting the house ablaze.
Local residents attempted to extinguish the flames, but the house was gutted.
Firefighters reached the scene around 11:15pm, by which time the fire had destroyed most of the property.
Chandpur Fire Service official Md Abdullah said most of the furniture had already been destroyed when firefighters arrived.

item.title: Dr Yunus’s ancestral house in Chittagong set on fire
item.description:
The ancestral house of former interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus was set on fire in Chittagong city around 11:30pm on Wednesday, amid incidents of sabotage allegedly involving leaders and activists of the banned Awami League across the country.
According to a report by Prothom Alo, the fire broke out in an abandoned room on the ground floor of the house in the city's Panchlaish area.
Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Panchlaish police station Mozammel Haque said police personnel were regularly patrolling the area when they noticed the fire and rushed to the spot. They later extinguished it.
Police are investigating who was involved in the incident, he said.
Responding to a question, Mozammel said nobody lives on the ground floor of the building, which remains abandoned. The families of Yunus's 2 brothers live on the second and third floors.
He added that security around the house had been strengthened following the incident.
A few days ago, miscreants set fire to 2 branches of Grameen Bank in Anwara and Satkania upazilas of Chittagong.
The main ancestral house of Grameen Bank founder Professor Yunus is located in Bathua village of Hathazari upazila in Chittagong. His father was a businessman, and through that connection, Yunus built the house in Panchlaish city.
Professor Yunus spent his childhood and adolescence in the Panchlaish house.

item.title: Crude bomb explosions at separate locations in capital, one detained
item.description:
Crude bomb explosions at separate locations in Dhaka on Wednesday evening left a woman seriously injured, while police detained one person in connection with twin explosions in Shyampur.
The incident in Shahjahanpur occurred on Wednesday, November 18, evening in front of Khilgaon Government Primary School, adjacent to Khilgaon Railgate Market, under Shahjahanpur police station.
Shahjahanpur police station Officer-in-Charge Amirul Islam said unidentified miscreants threw a crude bomb from atop the Khilgaon Flyover. It exploded on the road, seriously injuring nearby tea shop owner Nasima Begum, 40.
She was later admitted to Mugda Medical College Hospital.
Meanwhile, Shyampur police station Officer-in-Charge Md Nazrul Islam said twin crude bomb explosions occurred in front of the Dholai Par bus counter.
A person was caught red-handed at the time.

item.title: RMG unrest escalates, 300 arrested as clashes spread
item.description:
Garment workers’ protests demanding a Tk30,000 minimum monthly wage intensified across Dhaka, Gazipur, Savar and Ashulia on Wednesday, triggering fresh clashes with police, highway blockades and factory closures, while nearly 300 people have been arrested in connection with the continuing unrest.
The escalating confrontation, now in its third week, has disrupted production across Bangladesh’s largest export industry, with workers accusing authorities of delaying wage negotiations and police stepping up operations to contain the violence.
In Gazipur, thousands of workers blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway around 9am, bringing traffic to a standstill in Chhaydana, Hariken and surrounding industrial areas.
A vehicle belonging to Gazipur Metropolitan Police was set ablaze during clashes.
Police confirmed the arson, while law enforcement personnel worked to disperse protesters and restore traffic, which normalised after 2pm.
At least 20 factories in Savar and Ashulia remained closed amid the unrest, while several factories in Gazipur also suspended operations.
In Savar’s Ulail area, thousands of workers from Al-Muslim Group and nearby factories blocked the Dhaka-Aricha highway around 2:30pm.
Clashes erupted when police attempted to clear the road. Officers fired tear gas and rubber bullets after protesters allegedly threw bricks, forcing workers to retreat around 4pm.
Similar confrontations occurred in Ashulia’s Narsinghapur area, where police used tear gas to disperse workers attempting to block the Abdullahpur-Baipail road. Several people, including police personnel, were injured.
In the capital, garment workers clashed with police in Pallabi and became involved in confrontations with local BNP activists in Kafrul following allegations that female workers had been harassed.
Police used sound grenades to restore order.
Police said nearly 300 people had been arrested in 24 cases filed with Savar and Ashulia police stations over alleged sabotage during the continuing protests.
Two leaders of the Green Bangla Garments Workers Federation were also arrested in Dhaka on Tuesday night on allegations of inciting unrest.
The unrest intensified after the minimum wage board postponed its third meeting, scheduled for November 16. The meeting has now been rescheduled for November 23.
Workers are demanding an increase in the minimum wage from Tk12,500 to Tk30,000, arguing that rising living costs have eroded their purchasing power.
Labour leaders say uncertainty over the wage board’s proceedings has fuelled mistrust among workers, who want the new wage structure announced before December and implemented from December 1.
Meanwhile, lawmakers from both treasury and opposition benches have expressed support for a reasonable wage increase while alleging that vested interests, including elements linked to the ousted Awami League, are attempting to exploit the unrest.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told the National Parliament that some groups were deliberately prolonging the protests despite ongoing negotiations between workers and factory owners.

item.title: One public toilet for every 1.72 lakh people in Dhaka
item.description:
Dhaka has just one public toilet for every 172,641 residents, exposing a severe sanitation crisis in the densely populated capital, where inadequate facilities, poor maintenance and user fees are forcing many people to relieve themselves in public spaces while women increasingly restrict their water intake to avoid using toilets outside their homes.
According to the United Nations’ World Urbanization Prospects 2025, Dhaka’s estimated population stands at 36.6 million.
Yet data from Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) and Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) show only 219 public toilets, including mobile facilities.
Of these, three have been demolished and four remain closed, leaving 212 in the existing network, some of which are also not operational.
This translates to approximately 0.58 public toilets per 100,000 residents, highlighting the scale of the shortage on the World Toilet Day.
In his message marking World Toilet Day 2026, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said sanitation was a universal human right, stressing that safe and accessible toilets were essential to protecting women’s health, safety and dignity.
He noted that inadequate sanitation exposes millions of women and girls to risks, discourages them from eating and drinking while outside their homes, and restricts their participation in education, employment and public life.
DNCC records show 131 public toilets, including 81 established by the city corporation and eight mobile facilities primarily used for special events rather than regular public access.
Another 42 are operated by organisations including WaterAid Bangladesh, SPACE, BhumiJ and ARBAN.
DSCC has 88 public toilets, one of which, beside Shaheed Zia Shishu Park, has been demolished.
Among the closed facilities are toilets at Golartek Field in Mirpur-1, Gabtoli Sluice Gate, Mirpur Section 13 Park and Avenue 8 in Mirpur-11.
Photo: Ahadul Karim Khan/ Dhaka Tribune
Some have never opened despite completed construction, while others are undergoing renovation.
During visits to several public toilets, a Dhaka Tribune correspondent found missing soap and tissue paper, poor cleanliness and unpleasant smells.
Many facilities charged at least Tk10 per use.
The shortage is particularly difficult for an estimated two million drivers and transport workers who spend much of their working day on the streets.
During visits from Shewrapara through Farmgate to the University of Dhaka’s Teacher-Student Centre (TSC), the correspondent observed at least 30 people urinating beside roads and on footpaths.
Similar scenes were visible in Shahbagh, Kawran Bazar and Agargaon.
Sadman Hossain, a private-sector employee, described the situation near TSC as unbearable.
“I have to hold my breath while passing through this area. So many people are urinating openly on the footpaths, but there seems to be no one to look into it,” he said.
Another private-sector employee in Agargaon admitted urinating beside the road because he could not find a public toilet nearby.
Dhaka has an estimated 2 million rickshaw, van, CNG and other vehicle drivers and workers, many of whom spend most of their day on the streets.
The lack of affordable and accessible sanitation facilities particularly affects these groups.
For women, the shortage creates additional health, safety and dignity concerns.
Shahinur Begum said she deliberately reduces her water intake before leaving home to avoid needing a toilet.
“Once I am outside, I try not to drink water unless absolutely necessary because I might need to use a toilet,” she said.
Photo: Ahadul Karim Khan/ Dhaka Tribune
A WaterAid study, Women on the Go: How Poor Sanitation Influences Urban Women’s Water Intake in Bangladesh, found that 69% of women reduced their water consumption while outside, while another 15% avoided drinking water altogether.
Inspections at New Market, Mohakhali and Farmgate revealed broken door locks, unhygienic water containers, missing soap and tissue, and inadequate menstrual hygiene facilities.
At Mohakhali Inter-District Bus Terminal, several toilets previously designated for women have reportedly been converted into men’s facilities.
Ferdousi Begum, who travelled from Kishoreganj with her child, said she had no choice but to use an unhygienic toilet.
“It was not properly clean or suitable for use, but what else could I do?” she said.
Public health expert Dr Mushtuq Husain warned that inadequate sanitation increases the risk of infectious diseases and other health complications.
He said women who repeatedly delay urination may face urinary tract and bladder problems.
Urban planner Adil Mohammad Khan said public toilets should be treated as essential urban infrastructure, ideally available within every 400–500 metres.
He also questioned why residents must pay for such a basic necessity.
“People already pay taxes. Why should they have to pay for basic necessities?” he said.
DNCC Administrator Md Shafiqul Islam Khan Milton acknowledged that existing facilities were insufficient and said the corporation was working with WaterAid and other organisations to establish more toilets in high-demand areas.
“We recently held coordination meetings with WaterAid and other NGOs to discuss public toilets. We are working on establishing more facilities through a joint initiative involving the city corporation and WaterAid. We are prioritising areas with heavy public movement and where people face the greatest difficulties,” he told Dhaka Tribune.
DSCC Administrator Abdus Salam said the corporation was identifying locations for new toilets and strengthening monitoring of maintenance contractors.
“Thousands of people come to Dhaka every day from different parts of the country. We are trying to increase the number of public toilets and are already identifying locations where they are needed,” he told Dhaka Tribune.
“We are also taking steps to strengthen monitoring and address problems relating to cleanliness, maintenance and repairs,” he added.

item.title: Armed activists torch hospital, five BNP offices in Gopalganj
item.description:
Activists of the activities-banned Bangladesh Chhatra League staged armed demonstrations across Gopalganj town on Wednesday evening, attacking and setting fire to a private hospital. At least five BNP offices in the district were also torched during the day.
Witnesses said groups of activists carrying locally made weapons, including machetes and cleavers, rode motorcycles through Pachuria, the court area, Launch Ghat, Kachabazar intersection, Police Lines and Bedgram after 7:15pm.
The groups later gathered at Launch Ghat, where they chanted slogans under the leadership of Raju Khan, joint general secretary of the district Chhatra League.
Meanwhile, attackers led by Omar Faruk Khan Ripon, a former joint convener of the activities-banned organisation’s municipal unit, targeted Araf General Hospital and Diagnostic Centre, owned by Gopalganj-2 MP Dr KM Babar.
The attackers went live on Facebook as they vandalised the pathology unit, reception area and the lawmaker’s personal office on the ground floor of the five-storey building. They brought furniture outside, poured petrol on it and set it on fire. A crude bomb was also exploded during the attack.
Several patients, including pregnant women, women recovering from caesarean sections and newborns, were receiving treatment at the hospital. The attack triggered panic as relatives tried to move them to safety.
Separately, at least five BNP offices in different areas of Muksudpur Uupazila were set on fire between noon and evening. The Kashiani Upazila BNP Office and several union-level party offices were also attacked. Two Grameen Bank offices came under attack as well.
Earlier in the day, activists of the Awami League, Jubo League and Chhatra League staged demonstrations with machetes, Chinese axes and other locally made weapons at several points along the Gopalganj-Tungipara road. They also blocked six locations along the road by placing tree trunks and bamboo across it.

item.title: Crude bomb hurled at Khulna court building
item.description:
Miscreants threw a crude bomb at the ground floor of the Khulna District Judge Court building around 8:30pm on Wednesday, but it did not explode, causing no damage, police said.
Witnesses in the court area said two youths hurled the crude bomb before fleeing the scene. Police later visited the spot and recovered the unexploded device.
Khulna Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Lokman Hossain Ripon said that police recovered an unexploded crude bomb from the scene after receiving information.
“None could identify the attackers in the darkness. Efforts are underway to identify them,” he said.

item.title: Crude bomb hurled at Bogra Upazila Parishad premises
item.description:
A crude bomb was hurled at Bogra Sadar Upazila Parishad in the Matidali area of Bogra around 11pm on Tuesday.
