item.title: Gopalganj DC, SP transferred after armed procession, vandalism
item.description:
The government has transferred the deputy commissioner (DC) and superintendent of police (SP) of Gopalganj following an armed procession, vandalism and arson involving leaders and activists of the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned, and its affiliated organisations.
DC Md Arif-uz-Zaman has been withdrawn and attached to the Ministry of Public Administration, while SP Md Habibullah has been transferred to Feni.
Separate notifications issued by the Ministry of Public Administration and the Ministry of Home Affairs on Sunday confirmed the transfers.
GM Sarfaraz, currently serving as DC of Habiganj, has been appointed as the new DC of Gopalganj.
Feni SP Pratyush Kumar Majumder will replace Habibullah.
Earlier on Sunday, Awami League leaders and activists staged processions and rallies on several roads in Gopalganj town between 11am and 1:45pm.
The procession was organised to mobilise support for a lockdown program scheduled for November 19.
Many participants were seen carrying locally made weapons, including machetes, Chinese axes, spears, harpoons and bamboo poles.
The protesters broke through police barricades and entered different parts of the town. They vandalized the July Memorial and the signboard of Hadi Chattar at Gopalganj Science and Technology University.
The activists also unlocked the district Awami League office and put up a banner bearing the name “Government Bangabandhu College” at the entrance of Gopalganj Government College.
They also restored the university's Hadi Chattar to its former name, “Joy Bangla Chattar”.
Security was tightened across the district headquarters following the incidents, with members of the police, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), Special Response Battalion (SRB) and Armed Police Battalion (APBn) deployed at key locations.
Shops closed and the movement of rickshaws and vans was disrupted during the procession. The situation began to return to normal after 2pm.

item.title: Climate funding: Turning pledges into action remains a challenge
item.description:
Bangladesh has long been seeking increased international financing, technology transfer and support for climate adaptation to address the growing risks of climate change.
At COP31 in Antalya, Turkiye, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman placed five proposals before the international community, including allocating at least 50% of global climate finance to adaptation.
Meanwhile, Bangladesh has been invited to prepare an investment plan to seek up to $30 million under a new programme of the Climate Investment Funds (CIF).
However, the opportunity to seek funding does not guarantee that the money will be approved or disbursed.
Challenges remain in securing pledged funds, preparing investment proposals and ensuring that financial assistance reaches communities affected by climate change.
At the high-level segment of COP31 on November 12, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman presented five proposals to address the needs of climate-vulnerable countries.
He called for allocating at least 50% of international climate finance to adaptation, introducing debt-for-climate swaps and climate-resilient debt clauses to ease the debt burden of vulnerable nations, and ensuring equitable access to climate-friendly technologies through technology transfer.
The other proposals included expanding renewable energy through affordable financing and capacity development, and adopting the Belem-Antalya Action Mechanism to support a just energy transition based on equitable financing and trade.
The prime minister said climate-vulnerable countries needed grants rather than additional loans that would increase their debt burden. He also called for reliable financial support, access to modern technology and stronger assistance for adaptation.
He said the existing global climate financing system remained inadequate to meet the needs and priorities of developing countries.
Bangladesh has been invited to participate in the first phase of the Climate Investment Funds' (CIF) new Accelerating Resilience Investments and Strengthening Economies (ARISE) program.
Under the initiative, the country can prepare an investment plan to seek up to $30 million to strengthen climate resilience.
Environment, Forest and Climate Change State Minister Shaikh Faridul Islam disclosed the development to journalists on the third day of COP31 on November 12.
He said it was the first time such an announcement had been made at a climate conference.
The proposed funding could be used for ecosystem restoration, improving the livelihoods of coastal communities and constructing shelters in cyclone-prone areas, he said.
Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo said Bangladesh was expanding tree plantation and afforestation programs, promoting renewable energy, including solar power, and implementing environmentally sustainable development initiatives.
He said adequate and timely international financing was essential to implementing the country's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and National Adaptation Plan (NAP).
Prime Minister's Adviser Mahdi Amin said the government was prioritizing solar power to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and making solar energy mandatory in government and institutional buildings.
Initiatives were also underway to generate electricity from waste and promote electric vehicles to reduce emissions in the transport sector, he said.
He added that the government was encouraging industries to adopt environmentally friendly technologies, expanding green industries and increasing the coverage of LEED certification.
Other initiatives include a program to excavate and re-excavate 20,000 kilometres of rivers and canals and a target to plant 250 million trees over the next five years.
Steps have also been taken to implement the Padma Barrage and Teesta Master Plan to prevent groundwater wastage and improve integrated water resource management, he said.
Mahdi Amin said Bangladesh contributed negligibly to global carbon emissions but remained among the countries most vulnerable to climate change. International cooperation and compensation were therefore essential to address climate-related losses and damage.
Climate expert Professor Dr Ainun Nishat said securing financial commitments at climate conferences was not enough, stressing the need for proper monitoring and accountability to ensure that funds achieved their intended objectives.
He said previous climate conferences had produced several political and procedural commitments, but implementation remained a major challenge.
Bangladesh had so far received $464 million, while discussions were underway for another $30 million, he said.
However, he questioned whether the proposed funding would be used effectively, particularly given concerns over the capacity of the Water Development Board and the Ministry of Water Resources to manage projects in coastal areas.
Although the proposed amount was small compared with the needs of coastal communities, Bangladesh must demonstrate that it could use the money properly, he said. Otherwise, future funding could be affected.
Waterkeepers Bangladesh Coordinator Sharif Jamil said the proposed $30 million was negligible compared with the scale of damage suffered by coastal communities.
He said climate financing discussions had made limited progress compared with the needs of vulnerable countries. However, continued negotiations were important to hold countries accountable for climate change.
He also stressed the need to ensure that funds reached affected communities and benefited them directly, rather than focusing solely on announcing financial commitments.
Bangladesh's progress at COP31 will ultimately depend on whether funding pledges translate into actual disbursements, access to loss and damage financing improves and adequate support is secured for adaptation.
The real measure of success will be the amount of funding received and its impact on communities most vulnerable to climate change.

item.title: Kobir: Bangladesh, Türkiye hold fruitful talks on defence investment cooperation
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Sunday that the relationship between Bangladesh and Türkiye is now at a new height and the two countries had a fruitful discussion on investment partnership in the defence sector, particularly the possibility of investment in a defence industrial park and other areas of defence production.
“The Bangladesh-Türkiye relationship is at a new height and is moving towards a stronger and more comprehensive partnership. There was a fruitful discussion on investment partnership in the defence sector, particularly the possibility of investment in a defence industrial park and other areas of defence production,” he said.
The state minister made the remarks while responding to a question at a media briefing at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Foreign Secretary Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury and Additional Foreign Secretary (Public Diplomacy and Other Priority Matters) AKM Shahidul Karim were also present at the media briefing, which highlighted the outcomes of the prime minister’s visit to Türkiye in connection with COP31.
He said Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan expressed his willingness to work closely with Bangladesh and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to further strengthen bilateral relations, which are now moving towards a comprehensive partnership.
He said the bilateral meeting between the two leaders was held in a very cordial atmosphere, reflecting the growing importance Türkiye attaches to its relations with Bangladesh.
Kobir said Erdogan held bilateral meetings with only a handful of heads of government during the multilateral forum, making his meeting with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on the very first day particularly significant.
He said the Turkish president's decision to meet the Bangladesh prime minister amid his busy schedule reflected the importance he attached to Bangladesh and its leadership.
The state minister said the two sides had fruitful discussions on defence cooperation, including potential Turkish investment in a defence industrial park in Bangladesh and other areas of defence production.
On the Rohingya crisis, Kobir said the two leaders discussed the need for stronger international cooperation, particularly following the International Court of Justice (ICJ) verdict, to pursue the issue more vigorously.
They also discussed ways to strengthen international support for financing the humanitarian response to the Rohingya crisis , he said , describing the discussions as very positive.
The state minister said President Erdogan referred to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman as his “valued brother” and expressed his intention to work closely with him.
“Beyond being the leader of 180 million people in Bangladesh, you are my valued brother and a leader with whom I will work closely,” Kobir quoted the Turkish president as telling the prime minister .
Erdogan also assured the prime minister that Türkiye would extend all possible cooperation to Bangladesh and asked him to identify areas where such support would be needed, the state minister said.
Kobir said the bilateral relationship had reached a strong level at the highest political level and was expected to advance further through closer cooperation.
Responding to a question on climate finance, the state minister said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had placed particular emphasis on ensuring easier and faster access to climate funds for countries severely affected by climate change.
He said existing procedures for accessing climate finance were often lengthy and complicated, causing delays in the delivery of funds when vulnerable countries needed them most.
“Climate finance must be accessible. The procedures for accessing funds need to be made much easier so that the money reaches countries in time to address their environmental challenges,” he said.
Kobir said Bangladesh's position on easier access to climate finance was also shared by other countries facing the adverse effects of climate change .
He said the prime minister had highlighted the need to simplify the process so that climate-vulnerable countries could use the funds efficiently for environmental protection and disaster response.
The state minister also said negotiations at COP31 were still underway and the outcome document had yet to be finalised.
“We are working positively. The negotiations are still ongoing, and the outcome document has not yet been released,” he said.
The state minister described Prime Minister Tarique's participation in the COP31 World Leaders' Summit in Turkiye as highly successful, noting that the visit elevated Bangladesh's international standing and strengthened bilateral and multilateral cooperation.
"Taking everything into consideration, Bangladesh's participation in COP31 under the honourable prime minister's leadership was highly successful," he said.
Kobir said the visit provided an important opportunity to present the new government's commitments, priorities and vision to the international community while expanding Bangladesh's diplomatic engagement with key international partners.
"Through this visit, the prime minister, elected through the direct votes of the people after a long interval, has taken Bangladesh's confidence, honour and self-respect to a new height on the world stage," he said.
He said Bangladesh's participation was particularly significant as the country contributes less than 0.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions but remains among the nations most vulnerable to climate change.
Delivering Bangladesh's national statement at the COP31 plenary, Prime Minister Tarique highlighted climate justice, the historical responsibilities of developed countries, adaptation financing, loss and damage, and climate-resilient development.
The prime minister proposed allocating 50% of climate finance to adaptation and called for greater international cooperation to address climate-related loss and damage.
He also emphasised grant-based climate financing, technology transfer, a just energy transition and reforms to debt arrangements to support climate-vulnerable developing countries.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir stresses stronger Bangladesh-Qatar trade, investment ties
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Sunday expressed his desire to further strengthen bilateral ties by exploring the untapped potential for cooperation, particularly in the areas of trade and investment.
He also underscored Bangladesh’s interest in expanding the opportunities for skilled and semi-skilled Bangladeshi workers in Qatar.
The issues were discussed when Ambassador of the State of Qatar to Bangladesh, Seraya Ali Al Qahtani, met the state minister at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
During the meeting, the ambassador handed over an invitation from the Qatari State Minister, Dr Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Al Khulaifi, to attend an upcoming conference in Doha.
The state minister highlighted the longstanding and cordial relations between Bangladesh and Qatar. They also exchanged views on issues of mutual interest.
The Qatari ambassador appreciated the contribution of Bangladeshi workers to Qatar’s economy, noting their dedication, hard work and dignity.
Regarding the Rohingya crisis, the state minister thanked the Government of Qatar for its continued support and cooperation in various multilateral forums and sought its continued engagement towards a sustainable resolution of the crisis.

item.title: Minister: Nearly 500,000 workers go abroad since present govt took office
item.description:
Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury on Sunday told Parliament that nearly 500,000 Bangladeshi workers have so far been employed abroad after the present government assumed power in February last.
“Since the current government came to power, a total of 496,150 workers have been employed in different countries from February 17, 2026 to November 9, 2026,” he said.
Out of the total, 340,533 are skilled and semi-skilled workers, the minister said in his scripted answer to a question from treasury bench lawmaker Sarwar Jamal Nizam (Chittagong-13).
Earlier, the day’s sitting began at 4:20pm with Deputy Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal in the chair.
In reply to another question from the same lawmaker, the minister said Malaysia was one of the largest labour markets for Bangladeshi workers and the market, which had remained closed for a long time, had already reopened following the government's diplomatic efforts.
“Of the workers who could not go to Malaysia earlier, 1,545 have so far been sent there. The process of sending workers to Malaysia through the Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited (BOESL) completely free of cost has also begun,” he said.
Ariful said the government had received job demands for 568 workers, but a total of 4,029 aspiring migrant workers submitted applications (Against a demand for 120 workers), of whom 300 were initially selected through a lottery.
Replying to a third question from Nizam, he said his ministry had taken various plans and initiatives to expand overseas employment opportunities for Bangladeshi workers.
The minister said workers were being sent from Bangladesh to various countries, including Macedonia, Mauritius and Italy in Europe, as well as Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Singapore, Portugal, Seychelles, Serbia, Fiji and Romania.
The government would also take initiatives to appoint country-specific local lobbyists or consultants, as necessary, based on recommendations from Bangladesh missions abroad to expand employment opportunities, he said.
Ariful said Qatar was one of Bangladesh's major labour markets. The 7th meeting of the Joint Committee between Bangladesh and Qatar was held in Dhaka on May 18, 2026.
At the meeting, Qatar's labour minister expressed interest in recruiting Bangladeshi workers in various trades, including electrical work, plumbing, air-conditioning technology and welding.
“I hope it will be possible to send a larger number of workers to the country very soon,” Ariful said.
Regarding Japan, he said technical interns were being sent there completely free of cost under a memorandum of understanding, with the assistance of the International Manpower Development Organization (IM Japan).
Agreements had also been signed with seven other Japanese companies to facilitate the recruitment of Bangladeshi workers, the minister added.
He said workers were being regularly sent to Brunei, Jordan, South Korea, Japan, Hong Kong and several other countries at low or no cost through BOESL.
Ariful said the ministry had also taken initiatives, in line with the government's election manifesto and its action plan, to sign MoUs, Memorandums of Cooperation (MoCs) and other agreements with new destination countries.
Emphasising the importance of training to send more workers abroad, he said a project titled “Providing Driving Training for Employment at Home and Abroad” was underway to train 100,000 drivers.
He said a Foreign Language and Skills Centre had been launched at the Dhaka Technical Teachers Training Institute (DTTI) under the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET), considering the importance of teaching aspiring migrant workers the languages of their destination countries.
Training programmes in Japanese, Korean, English, Chinese (Cantonese and Mandarin), Arabic, Italian and German, among other languages, have already been introduced through the recruitment of trainers, said the minister.

item.title: Chittagong RRF SP Jahangir Alam placed on 4-day remand in sedition case
item.description:
A Chittagong court has placed Jahangir Alam, superintendent of police (SP) of the Chittagong Range Reserve Force (RRF), on a four-day remand in a sedition case.
Chittagong Metropolitan Magistrate Mohammad Mostafa passed the order on Sunday afternoon.
Advocate Mofizul Haque Bhuiyan, public prosecutor (PP) of the Chittagong Metropolitan Magistrate Court, told Dhaka Tribune that police had sought a seven-day remand to interrogate Jahangir in the case. After hearing the petition, the court granted four days.
Jahangir is the son of Jinnat Ali of Chandapasha village in Shibpur upazila of Narsingdi. He lived at the Chittagong Police Officers' Mess in the city's Panchlaish area.
Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Abul Kashem Chowdhury of the RRF filed the case against Jahangir, accusing him of maintaining links with the banned Awami League.
The case was filed with Panchlaish Police Station around 10:30pm on Saturday after obtaining approval from the Home Ministry. Later that night, members of the Special Response Unit (SRU), Counter Terrorism Unit and Panchlaish police arrested him.
Earlier, authorities had seized his personal and official mobile phones over allegations of links with the Awami League and placed him under surveillance.
He was produced before the court on Sunday amid tight security.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,314 as eight die in 24 hrs
item.description:
Eight more people have died with measles-like symptoms across the country in the 24 hours from 8am Saturday to 8am Sunday, although no deaths from confirmed measles were reported during the period.
Meanwhile, 1,572 people were reported to have either suspected or confirmed measles infections, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
In a press release, the DGHS said 1,209 people had died with measles-like symptoms since March 15. Another 105 died after testing positive for measles, bringing the total death toll from confirmed measles and measles-like symptoms to 1,314.
Of the 1,572 cases reported in the past 24 hours, 1,414 were suspected measles cases, while 158 were confirmed.
Since March 15, a total of 221,539 suspected measles patients have been admitted to hospitals across the country. Of them, 212,402 have recovered and been discharged.
The DGHS data further showed that 248,060 people had developed measles-like symptoms during the period, while 25,269 cases had been confirmed as measles.

item.title: Humaiun: Bangladesh, Turkiye moving towards comprehensive partnership
item.description:
Bangladesh and Turkiye are moving towards a comprehensive partnership following highly productive talks between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, particularly on defense investment, industrial cooperation and the Rohingya crisis.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir made the remarks at a media briefing here today, describing the bilateral meeting between the two leaders on the sidelines of the COP31 World Leaders' Summit in Antalya as exceptionally cordial and significant.
"Bangladesh-Turkiye relations have reached a new high. We are moving towards a stronger and more comprehensive partnership," he said.
The state minister said the two leaders held fruitful discussions on expanding defense cooperation, including potential Turkish investment in Bangladesh's defense industrial park and other areas of defense manufacturing.
"Defense cooperation was discussed in terms of defense investment, possible investment in the defense industrial park, and other areas of defense production," he said.
Humaiun Kobir said the discussions were particularly encouraging regarding the prospects of developing an investment partnership between the two countries.
Highlighting the significance of the meeting, he said President Erdogan had held bilateral talks with only a limited number of visiting heads of government despite his demanding schedule as host of the international climate summit.
"One of the most prominent bilateral meetings on the very first day was with our Honorable Prime Minister Tarique Rahman," he said.
The state minister said the priority accorded to the meeting demonstrated the importance the Turkish President attached to Bangladesh and its leadership in international political and economic affairs.
He said the two leaders also discussed strengthening cooperation on the Rohingya crisis, including international legal efforts, humanitarian financing and coordinated diplomatic initiatives.
Humaiun said both sides explored ways to work more effectively together to address the crisis amid growing concerns over declining international assistance for Rohingya refugees.
"Very positive discussions took place," he said, referring to cooperation on the Rohingya issue and financing the humanitarian response.
The state minister said President Erdogan had expressed strong personal warmth towards Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and reaffirmed his commitment to strengthening relations with Bangladesh.
Quoting the Turkish President, Humaiun said Erdogan told the prime minister: "You are my valued brother. You are the leader of the 180 million people of Bangladesh, but beyond that, you are my valued brother and leader with whom I will work closely."
According to Humaiun Kobir, Erdogan also assured the prime minister of Turkiye's willingness to extend cooperation to Bangladesh in areas within its capacity.
"Whatever is within my capacity and Turkiye's capacity for Bangladesh, I will do it. You just need to let me know where and what needs to be done," Humaiun quoted the Turkish President as saying.
The state minister described the relationship between the two countries as exceptionally strong at the highest political level.
He expressed optimism that the understanding reached during the meeting would help advance cooperation in defense production, investment and humanitarian diplomacy.
"The relationship is exceptionally wonderful, at a high-powered and strong level, and it will move forward, Insha'Allah," Humaiun Kobir said.

item.title: Wahid-Uz-Zaman appointed new BTRC chairman
item.description:
Major General (retd) Md Wahid-Uz-Zaman has been appointed chairman of the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) for one year on a contractual basis, replacing Major General Md Emdad Ul Bari.
The remaining tenure of Emdad Ul Bari's contractual appointment as BTRC chairman has been cancelled.
The Ministry of Public Administration issued two separate notifications in this regard on Sunday.
According to the notification on the new appointment, Wahid-Uz-Zaman has been appointed under Section 49 of the Government Service Act, 2018, subject to the suspension of his post-retirement leave and related benefits and relinquishment of any other professional or business engagement, as well as employment with any government, semi-government or private institution or organization.
He has been appointed on a contractual basis as commissioner (management and administration) of the BTRC and posted as its chairman for one year from the date of his joining.
Other terms and conditions of the appointment will be determined through a contract, the notification said.

item.title: 41 platoons of BGB deployed in industrial areas, Gopalganj
item.description:
A total of 41 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) were deployed in key industrial areas of Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj, as well as in Gopalganj, on Sunday to maintain law and order, ensure public safety and prevent any untoward incidents.
Of the total deployment, 18 platoons are operating in Savar and Ashulia of Dhaka, 10 in different industrial areas of Gazipur and seven in Narayanganj, according to a BGB statement.
In Gazipur, BGB personnel are working in Chandra, Palli Bidyut, Mouchak, Konabari, Telirchala, Kashimpur, Bhogra Bypass, Gachha, Sataish and Salna areas.
In Narayanganj, the deployment covers Shibu Market, Katherpool, Jalkuri, BSCIC Industrial Estate, Chashara intersection, Kanchpur Bridge and Shimrail.
The deployed BGB members are maintaining vigilance in coordination with local administration and police to ensure security and stability in the industrial zones, said BGB Public Relations Officer Shariful Islam.
Besides, six platoons of BGB were deployed in Gopalganj to maintain law and order in the district.
They are carrying out their assigned duties in coordination with other law enforcement agencies in line with the requirements and advice of the district magistrate.
BGB members are maintaining the highest level of vigilance and professionalism to ensure overall security and stability.

item.title: 13 garment factories closed indefinitely in Gazipur amid workers' unrest
item.description:
Authorities have announced the indefinite closure of 13 garment factories in Gazipur amid workers' unrest, while five other factories have declared a holiday for Sunday.
Additional law enforcement personnel have been deployed at key points across the industrial zone to prevent further unrest, Gazipur Industrial Police-2 Superintendent of Police Mohammad Amjad Hossain said.
According to the Industrial Police, several garment factories in the Mouchak area of Kaliakair declared a holiday at around 8:45am. After leaving their workplaces, workers staged a procession and gathered in front of Hydro Oxide Limited.
When the workers attempted to block the Dhaka-Tangail highway, police intervened and dispersed them, preventing further escalation.
A notice issued by the management of factories under Apex Holding Limited, signed by its assistant general manager for administration and human resources, said the company had made efforts to maintain normal production despite the unrest and instability in the surrounding industrial areas following the government's announcement of a minimum wage increase.
The notice said the factories had opened as scheduled on Saturday, but workers had refused to perform their assigned duties, disrupting production.
Citing the prevailing situation and Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006, the management announced the suspension of operations across all departments and branches from Sunday, November 15, for an indefinite period.
The notice said the date for reopening would be announced later and asked all concerned to comply with the decision.
Far East Knitting and Dyeing Industries in the Purba Chandra area of Kaliakair also announced an indefinite closure on Sunday. The factory employs several thousand workers.
In its notice, the management said the decision followed vandalism and attacks on factory staff and officials amid unrest over minimum wage demands.
It alleged that, despite communications from the government and the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) regarding the approval and implementation of the new minimum wage, the unrest had escalated, with outsiders allegedly instigating destructive activities.
According to the notice, protesters entered the factory premises and vandalised the facility, causing extensive damage and injuring several workers and officials.
The management said operations had been suspended under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006.
Other factories reported closed indefinitely include Ecotex Limited and Ahsan Composite in the Chandra Palli Bidyut area, as well as several units under Apex Holding: Apex Spinning and Knitting Mills Ltd, Apex Textiles Printing Mills Ltd, Apex Lingerie Ltd and its extension, Apex Yarn Dyeing Ltd, and Apex Fashion Wear Ltd.
Moazuddin Textile Limited in the Mouchak area has also been closed indefinitely.
Amjad Hossain said the situation had remained largely normal during the morning. However, shortly after 8:30am, workers from Lavenda garment factory in the Telirchala area of Mouchak arrived for their shifts but did not start work.
Instead, they took to the highway and staged a blockade, halting traffic for around half an hour.
He said protesters threw bricks and stones at police when they were asked to clear the road. Police then fired tear gas shells to disperse them.
The workers fled the scene, and traffic returned to normal at around 9am, he added.

item.title: Bangladesh, Sri Lanka discuss expediting trade, investment negotiations
item.description:
Bangladesh and Sri Lanka on Sunday discussed expediting ongoing negotiations to promote bilateral trade and investment as part of efforts to strengthen cooperation between the two countries.
The discussion took place when Sri Lankan High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dharmapala Weerakkody paid a courtesy call on State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Dhaka, said a ministry press release.
During the meeting, they reviewed ongoing bilateral cooperation, including initiatives to expand trade and investment through faster progress in negotiations.
Kobir said Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, under their new leaderships, were pursuing nation-building in a pragmatic and forward-looking manner.
He underscored the mutual interest in exploring all possible avenues of cooperation to fulfill the aspirations of the peoples of both countries.
The state minister also recalled his interactions with Sri Lankan leaders on the sidelines of multilateral events.
He stressed the need to implement the decisions of the fourth Bangladesh-Sri Lanka Foreign Office Consultation held in Colombo in November 2025. The next consultation will take place in Dhaka.
Both sides expressed optimism about further deepening the longstanding and multifaceted relations between the two countries.

item.title: Govt cuts import duties on dates, oranges and apples ahead of Ramadan
item.description:
The government on Sunday said import duties on imported dates, oranges, and apples would be reduced temporarily, coinciding with the holy month of Ramadan.
According to an official statement, the cabinet, in its 27th meeting with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in the chair, decided to reduce duty on imported dates to 5% from 25%, while the rate would remain in effect until March 10, 2027.
It said the import tax on oranges (malta) under HS Code 08051010 and apples under HS Code 08081010 was set at 61%, down from the existing 121.78%, while the makeshift arrangement would remain effective from January 24 to February 23.
The statement said the cabinet gave in-principle and final approval to a revenue board (NBR) proposal to revert from the quarterly setup introduced in the 2026-27 budget, asking standard businesses to submit VAT returns within 15 days of the end of each monthly tax period.
The revised provision is expected to be incorporated in the proposed “Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty (Amendment) Act, 2026” amending an October 2026 ordinance introducing quarterly VAT filing with monthly submissions.
It recalled that the budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year had relaxed the requirement of submitting VAT returns every month, allowing submission within 15 days of the end of every three months in line with the ordinance.
The statement said the change created obstacles for revenue collection at the field level, making it necessary to amend Section 64 of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012.
The amendment is expected to be approved at the current parliament session, subject to Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division vetting.

item.title: PM advises students to maintain cleanliness, show kindness to animals
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has advised students to maintain cleanliness, plant trees and treat all animals, including birds, with kindness and compassion.
He gave the advice during an interaction with students from several educational institutions at the National Parliament on Sunday.
During a recess in the parliamentary session, the students paid a courtesy call on the prime minister.
The delegation included 41 students who secured GPA-5 in the 2026 HSC examinations from various educational institutions in Patgram and Hatibandha upazilas of Lalmonirhat, along with six teachers and guardians.
Also present were 27 students from grades 10 and 11 and six teachers from The Aga Khan Academy, as well as 41 students and two teachers from the Department of Law at Brac University.
During the interaction, the prime minister expressed hope that the younger generation would take an interest in politics and state governance. However, he advised them to first develop themselves as qualified, skilled and responsible citizens before becoming involved in politics.
He offered three specific suggestions to the students.
First, he urged them to keep their cities, homes and surrounding areas clean and dispose of waste in designated places rather than littering.
Second, he encouraged them to plant at least one tree during the monsoon season to mark their own birthdays or those of family members.
Third, he called on them to show kindness and compassion towards all animals, including birds.
Earlier, the students attended a briefing at the National Parliament. They also visited the parliamentary library and observed a session of parliament. Later, they took part in a photo session at the North Plaza of the parliament building.
Information Minister Andalib Rahman, State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam, Prime Minister's Press Secretary Saleh Shibli, Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Ruman and Prime Minister's Private Secretary-2 Mehedul Islam were also present.

item.title: Dengue: 8 more die, 1,952 hospitalized in 24hrs
item.description:
Eight people died of dengue and 1,952 new patients were hospitalised across the country in the 24 hours to Sunday morning.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll has risen to 499 in the country this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the new deaths, five were recorded in Dhaka division, while one each in Mymensingh, Chittagong and Khulna divisions.
Since January 1 this year, a total of 162,509 dengue patients have been admitted to hospitals across the country. Of them, 156,194 have recovered.
Currently, 5816 patients are receiving treatment at different hospitals across the country.

item.title: Sabalenka sorry for outburst in Svitolina defeat
item.description:
Aryna Sabalenka apologized on Saturday after an on-court outburst during her defeat to Ukrainian rival Elina Svitolina at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells.
Footage shared widely on social media appeared to show the former world number one swearing in a tirade that some commenters interpreted as directed towards Svitolina or Ukrainians in general.
However, Sabalenka said Saturday that she lost her cool due to the behavior of spectators during Friday's 3-6, 6-3, 1-6 defeat, which sent the four-time Grand Slam-winner crashing out.
"I want to clarify something from my recent match that has been circulating online," Sabalenka wrote in a post on Instagram.
"My comment was not directed at Elina. I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes and I reacted emotionally in the moment.
"That said, I should have handled my frustration differently and I apologise to anyone I offended. Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament."
Svitolina, who has refused to shake hands with tennis players from Russia and its regional ally Belarus since Moscow's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, acknowledged that a match against Sabalenka could carry extra weight for her fans.
"As we see there's many, many Ukrainians, many, many flags ... and of course they want me to win this particular match," she said Saturday when asked about Sabalenka's statement.
"We've played many times with Aryna ... she has her fans. I have my fans," added Svitolina, who reached the Finals title match with a win over Linda Noskova on Saturday.
"I have seen the glimpse of it because obviously it's in the social media," she said. "(I) just hope the matches between us (are) respected. Sometimes in some matches that we've played also there have been not great comments towards me in regards of the war.
"It is like this in the social media sometimes the things are turned around a little bit."

item.title: Andreeva beats Pegula to book WTA Finals title clash with Svitolina
item.description:
French Open winner Mirra Andreeva beat Jessica Pegula 6-3, 6-4 on Saturday to book a WTA Finals title showdown with former champion Elina Svitolina in Indian Wells, California.
Ukraine's Svitolina, who won the WTA Finals in 2018, fell to Ashleigh Barty in the final in the following year but hadn't been back since, powered past Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova 6-2, 6-1 to give herself a shot at another triumph in the elite season-ending event.
"It's really magical to be back in the finals," Svitolina said. "Just very special for me to have this opportunity (Sunday), to have another battle another challenge."
The 32-year-old, back in the top 10 this year for the first time since before her daughter, Skai, was born in 2022, will face a rising star in 19-year-old Andreeva.
The Russian teen won her maiden major at Roland Garros this year and with her victory over Pegula is assured of rising from third to second in the world rankings.
Andreeva remained unbeaten in her WTA Finals singles debut, having posted round robin victories over sixth-ranked Svitolina, world number two Aryna Sabalenka and Diana Shnaider.
She's the youngest player to make the final since a 17-year-old Maria Sharapova in 2004 and joined Serena Williams and Chris Evert as the only players to win their first four matches in the event in straight sets.
"I think I can be very proud of myself," she told Tennis Channel. "I'm very happy with how I'm playing. I'm very happy also with how I deal with the pressure. I knew this match had a lot on the line."
For Pegula it was a match of missed chances, the fifth-ranked American unable to build on early breaks in both sets.
Andreeva double-faulted on break point to give Pegula a 2-1 lead in the opening set.
But the Russian broke back immediately, whipping a crosscourt forehand winner on her third break chance to make it 2-2.
Andreeva saved a pair of break points in the fifth game and broke again for a 5-3 lead.
Pegula had a chance to extend the set in the next game, but on break point she smashed what looked to be an easy backhand at the net past the baseline and Andreeva held to pocket the first.
Andreeva double-faulted to give Pegula a break chance in the fourth game of the second and the American converted for an imposing 3-1 lead.
But once again Andreeva broke back immediately, winning five of the last six games to close out the victory in one hour and 25 minutes.
Svitolina said she did "pretty much everything" well against Noskova, who crumbled with 11 double faults as the Ukrainian surged to victory in just 65 minutes.
The Czech is second on the WTA Tour's aces list behind Elena Rybakina but had just two -- the second to save a match point in the penultimate game.
Noskova took the game, but it was a brief reprieve. In the next Svitolina took the match on her third match point when a Noskova forehand slid wide.
"I think I played really well today, serving good, returning well, too," Svitolina said. "I was able to play aggressive and find the angles."
The round robin format means Svitolina will have the chance, rare in tennis, of avenging her lopsided Monday loss to Andreeva in the same tournament.
"She's in good form, but I feel like I've found my game since I lost the first match against her," Svitolina said. "I will do my homework with my coaches and try to find the key."

item.title: How do I grieve someone I have not met yet?
US air travel resumption will ‘take time’ after hours-long stop
69 primary schools running without headteachers in Sariakandi

High Court issues directives to control noise pollution
item.description:
The High Court Division has issued interim directives to control noise pollution, including regulating the use of fireworks and unnecessary vehicle horns and conducting regular drives in designated silent zones.
A Division Bench comprising Justice Sikder Mahmudur Razi and Justice Fatema Anwar issued the directives following a preliminary hearing of a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers Association (BELA), registered as case No 14939/2026.
The court also issued a rule asking the authorities concerned to explain why their failure to control noise pollution under existing laws and policies should not be declared illegal, contrary to public interest and public safety, and a violation of citizens' constitutional right to life under Articles 31 and 32.
The rule also seeks an explanation on why directions should not be issued to formulate and implement a coordinated, time-bound action plan to control noise pollution in silent zones and pollution caused by construction work, industrial establishments, social events, festivals and vehicles.
The court issued the following interim directives to the Inspector General of Police, director general of the Department of Environment, chairmen of the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA) and Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (RAJUK), commissioner of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), and administrators of Dhaka North and Dhaka South City Corporations:
The court directed the authorities concerned to submit reports on compliance with the directives every 3 months.
The respondents in the case include the secretaries of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and the Road Transport and Highways Division under the Ministry of Road Transport and Bridges; the Inspector General of Police; the DMP commissioner; the director general of the Department of Environment; the chairmen of BRTA and RAJUK; and the administrators of Dhaka North and Dhaka South City Corporations.
Dhaka, home to more than 2.2 crore people, frequently ranks among the world's most noise-polluted cities. Major sources of noise include unnecessary honking and hydraulic horns, industrial activities, construction work, generators, loud music at social events, uncontrolled use of microphones and loudspeakers, and fireworks.
Under the Noise Pollution (Control) Rules, 2025, areas within 100 meters of hospitals, educational institutions, offices and courts are designated as silent zones. The rules also regulate the use of fireworks and firecrackers and empower police to control prohibited vehicle horns.
In Dhaka, designated silent zones include a 3km radius around Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, the Secretariat and surrounding areas, Agargaon, the Parliament Building, the Prime Minister's Office area, Dhaka North City Corporation, Gulshan, Banani, Baridhara and Niketan.
BELA filed the case citing continued violations of prescribed noise levels in these areas and a lack of effective monitoring by the relevant authorities.
Md Ashraf Ali, Barrister-at-Law, represented BELA in the case, assisted by Advocate Hasanul Banna.

item.title: Gazipur garment workers return to work; security tightened
item.description:
Security has been tightened across Gazipur's industrial belt following recent workers' unrest over demands for a higher minimum wage, with 25 platoons of law enforcement personnel deployed under the supervision of 25 executive magistrates.
Workers began returning to their duties at various garment factories on Sunday morning. No fresh incidents of protests or road blockades had been reported in the industrial areas as of 8:30am. However, authorities have declared a holiday at six garment factories as a precautionary measure.
Arif Hossain, assistant commissioner of the Media and Research Cell at the Gazipur Deputy Commissioner's Office, confirmed the information on Sunday morning.
He said 13 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), five platoons of Ansar and eight platoons of the Special Response Battalion (SRB) had been deployed to maintain law and order. The forces are operating under the supervision of 25 executive magistrates.
Arif added that law enforcement agencies remained on high alert to prevent damage to public and private property or disruption to public life. BGB personnel had already begun operations, while other units remained on standby.
Earlier, garment workers in different parts of Gazipur staged protests and blocked the Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways, demanding an increase in the minimum wage.
During the unrest, incidents of arson were reported at police outposts, police vehicles and factory warehouses. Several clashes also broke out between protesters and law enforcement personnel, leaving workers and members of the security forces injured. Several people were detained in connection with the incidents.
Following the unrest, a number of garment factories in Gazipur announced holidays.
Meanwhile, a worker named Taufiq died after being beaten while recording the protests on his mobile phone.

item.title: Chittagong RRF SP arrested over alleged Awami League links, information leak
item.description:
Jahangir Alam, superintendent of police (SP) of the Chittagong Range Reserve Force (RRF), has been arrested in a sedition case over allegations of maintaining contact with the now-banned Awami League and leaking sensitive police information.
His personal and official mobile phones had been seized, and he was placed under surveillance before his arrest.
Following approval from the Ministry of Home Affairs, RRF Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Abul Kashem Chowdhury filed a case against him at Panchlaish police station around 10:30pm on Saturday. Later that night, a joint team of the Special Response Unit (SRU), Counter-Terrorism Unit and Panchlaish police arrested him at the Officers' Mess.
Chittagong Metropolitan Police (CMP) Commissioner Hasan Shawkat Ali confirmed the arrest, saying the Ministry of Home Affairs had approved the action on Friday.
According to police sources, Chittagong Range Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Abdul Kuddus Chowdhury questioned Jahangir last Tuesday after preliminary evidence of the alleged incident emerged.
His personal and official mobile phones were seized the same day and sent to the police Special Branch (SB) headquarters in Dhaka for forensic examination.
Meanwhile, an internal departmental investigation is underway, led by Shafijul Islam, additional DIG (Operations) of the Chittagong Range.
Sources at the Chittagong Range office said Jahangir had been summoned over allegations that he shared internal and sensitive police information with Awami League leaders and activists, despite the party's activities being currently prohibited.
Citing the first information report (FIR), a CMP official told the media that a message allegedly sent from Jahangir's mobile phone referred to people taking to the streets in December, describing them as swarming "like bees".
The message also reportedly referred to his participation in the 1996 movement demanding a caretaker government and expressed support for the ideals of Bangabandhu. It further included a statement about "rescuing" Bangladesh.
However, the identity of the message's recipient has not been established.
Sources said the investigation could be assigned to a specialised police unit, such as the SRU or the Counter-Terrorism Unit.

Korail slum fire leaves one dead
item.description:
A young man was killed, and at least 7-8 shanties and a shop were gutted in a fire at the T&T Colony of the capital's Korail slum early Sunday.
The deceased was identified as Shahriar Rahman Shuvro, 19, son of Md Monir Hossain. Hailing from Shirjugh village in Jhalakathi Sadar upazila, he was a tenant of one Islam at Satellite Gate in T&T Colony.
Duty officer at the Fire Service and Civil Defence control room Rakibul Hasan said they received information about the fire at 4:53am and immediately dispatched three units to the spot.
The fire was brought under control around 6am, he said, adding that one person was killed in the incident.
The cause of the fire and the extent of the damage were not immediately known.
